Berdasarkan laporan, for more than 30 years, the paper covered an increasingly repressive russia. “The process of silencing us started many years ago,” one of its journalists said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, outside a five-story office building on potapovsky lane in moscow, a group of journalists took down a metal plaque and installed a plastic one in its place: novaya gazeta lived here. White carnations, the flower that Russians associate with mourning, were placed on top of it.

Novaya Gazeta, Russia’s most daring independent newspaper for decades, closed its doors on Monday, the latest blow to Russians who value freedom of expression and human rights.

Sebagaimana diketahui, its forced closure is emblematic of the kremlin’s erasure of opinions, ideas and people that do not conform to its views. That process has been underway for years, but it has dramatically accelerated since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Sebagaimana diketahui, novaya gazeta’s journalists were packing up their offices when i visited on monday. Its co-founder Dmitri A. Muratov, who shared the Nobel Peace Prize in 2021 for defending press freedom, was giving away personal items to colleagues and well-wishers.

Berdasarkan laporan, he handed his emerald banker’s lamp to one of the paper’s last recruits, a video journalist. He kept for himself a fire evacuation floor plan, on which he asked staff members to sign their names where their offices had been.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but on sunday, greene was featured on cbs’ “60 minutes” in an interview the long-running show promoted on twitter with the tease: “republican rep. She sits down with Lesley Stahl this Sunday on 60 Minutes. Marjorie Taylor Greene, nicknamed MTG, isn’t afraid to share her opinions, no matter how intense and in-your-face they are. ” The images attached to this tweet by “60 Minutes” include Greene and Stahl walking through the US Capitol, taking a stroll outside and Greene showing Stahl something on her phone.

It's time for Marjorie Taylor Greene to go.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the segment that aired sunday night, stahl noted the congresswoman had moved from the fringe to the gop’s front row in two years despite a “sharp tongue” and “some pretty radical views” as well as “over the top” comments such as “the democrats are a party of pedophiles. But Stahl didn’t mention Greene spoke at a white nationalist event a year ago while a member of Congress or her extreme anti-Muslim views and her defense of January 6 rioters.

Berdasarkan laporan, criticism of cbs for amplifying greene has been swift and well-deserved even before the program aired. Insane that 60 min would do this. Former GOP Rep. ” (Kinzinger is a CNN senior political commentator. Adam Kinzinger of Illinois tweeted beforehand: “Wow. ).

Sebagaimana diketahui, journalist molly jong-fast also slammed “60 minutes” with the tweet: “attention is currency and 60 minutes is spending its currency on the jewish space lasers woman. ” (Jong-Fast was apparently referring to Greene’s past claim that a massive California wildfire was started by “a laser” beamed from space controlled by a prominent Jewish banking family. ).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, david hogg, who survived the 2018 horrific school shooting at marjory stoneman douglas high school in parkland and has since become an activist against gun violence, responded, “i look forward to your questions about why she thinks school shootings are fake and why she’s supported qanon. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, greene amplified the conspiracy theory — two years before being elected to congress — that the parkland shooting that took 17 lives was staged. Sebagaimana diketahui, now, it is true that “60 minutes” over its 50-plus-year history has featured what the show has dubbed “controversial” guests. These include a 2000 interview with Oklahoma City bomber Timothy McVeigh, whose 1995 terrorist attack left 168 dead, including 19 children. And the show did a 1979 interview with Iran’s Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, perhaps “60 minutes” views greene — who has repeatedly downplayed and even defended the january 6, 2021, attack plus called for the gop to become the party of “christian nationalism” — in the vein of its long list of controversial guests. (CBS had not responded to a request from CNN for comment at time of publishing. ).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, however, the choice of greene as a guest instantly recalls the comments of then-cbs ceo les moonves during trump’s 2016 presidential campaign when he admitted that trump’s candidacy “may not be good for america, but it’s damn good for cbs. … (T)his is going to be a very good year for us,” concluding, “Sorry. Diungkapkan bahwa moonves may be gone from cbs, but it appears his mindset continues at “60 minutes. ” And that may be good for “60 Minutes,” but it’s definitely not good for America.

Sebagaimana diketahui, sonia gandhi standing in front of the desk of her late husband and the former prime minister, rajiv gandhi, at their residence in new delhi in november. Credit. Saumya Khandelwal for The New York Times.

The astonishing story of Sonia Gandhi, the young woman from a middle-class Italian family who married into the Nehru-Gandhi dynasty, lived through unspeakable tragedy and nearly became prime minister of India, reached a crescendo in May 2004 in her heavily fortified home in New Delhi.

“It took place in this very room,” she said in an interview last week in her home office, once that of her late husband, Rajiv Gandhi.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on that day in 2004, party elders beseeched sonia gandhi, criticized by the opposition as a foreign-born interloper, to take her place as prime minister as the leader of the congress party, which had just won national elections. She initially said yes, horrifying her two children, Rahul and Priyanka, but recanted.

“My brother and I actually thought that she would get killed, too,” said Priyanka Gandhi, who sat next to her mother in the interview.

#256. These are the animals people most want to see photographed

📅 03 Apr 2023

These are the animals people most want to see photographed

Tanggal: 03 Apr 2023 | Sumber: https://www.cnn.com/travel/article/new-big-5-wildlife-photography-book-c2e-scn-spc-intl/index.html

Diungkapkan bahwa editor’s note:  call to earth is a cnn editorial series committed to reporting on the environmental challenges facing our planet, together with the solutions. Rolex’s Perpetual Planet initiative has partnered with CNN to drive awareness and education around key sustainability issues and to inspire positive action.

Berdasarkan laporan, originally a term used by trophy hunters in africa, the “big five” described the animals most challenging to shoot and kill: the lion, elephant, leopard, rhino, and buffalo. Nowadays, it is more loosely used to refer to some of Africa’s largest and most iconic animals.

Diungkapkan bahwa however, british photographer graeme green has reclaimed the narrative, creating a global “new big five” for wildlife photography. In 2021, 50,000 people around the world voted for the five animals they would most like to photograph, or see photographed, in the wild. Five animals were crowned the winners: the elephant, polar bear, lion, gorilla and tiger.

This week, sees the publication of “The New Big 5” photography book, which features images of those animals and other at-risk wildlife, from photography legends such as Ami Vitale, Steve McCurry and Paul Nicklen, and essays from famous conservationists and activists including like Jane Goodall and Paula Kahumbu.

Green says that the book celebrates wildlife and is a global call to action on issues impacting wildlife, including habitat loss, poaching, pollution and climate change.

Green was on assignment in Botswana at least a decade ago when he came up with the idea for a project to encourage people to “shoot with a camera, not a gun,” he says.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i thought this would be a way to get people really focusing on wildlife, thinking about the wildlife they love, thinking about the animals that are at risk. ”.

Ten photographs that made the world wake up to climate change.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in total, the book includes the work of 144 globally renowned wildlife photographers from ecuador to india. Curating the images took nearly two years of work, says Green.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i think these are some of the most beautiful and creative images that i’ve seen put together in one book,” says green. “These are the species that we are at risk of losing. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa according to the un, nature is declining at an unprecedented rate, with around one million of the planet’s animal and plant species facing extinction. The “New Big 5,” all of which are threatened, act as ambassadors for what is happening in the natural world, says Green.

Berdasarkan laporan, as well as being a powerful reminder of what we stand to lose, the book also points people towards potential solutions. Featured essays explore the benefits of rewilding and the importance of indigenous communities in conservation.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a chapter on endangered species from bees to blue whales illustrates the alarming threat climate change poses to animals outside of the “new big 5. ” “That’s only the tip of the iceberg – I could have included thousands of pictures because that’s how serious the situation is,” says Green.

Why a wildlife photographer took 40,000 photos to capture these extraordinary birds.

Jane Goodall, a leading conservationist who also wrote the afterword to the book, said in a press release that “we have a window of time during which we can start to heal some of the harm we have inflicted on the natural world, but only if we get together and take action now.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i hope the photos will lead people into the wonderful worlds of these iconic species. Then, perhaps, other people will become involved in helping to create a world where wildlife can flourish for future generations to enjoy,” she said.

“The New Big 5: A Global Photography Project For Endangered Wildlife,” by Graeme Green, published by Earth Aware Editions, is on sale from April 4, 2023.

This story has been updated to reflect the range of issues covered by the book.

#262. Study finds slightly higher risk of autism diagnosis in areas with more lithium in drinking water, but experts say more research is needed

📅 03 Apr 2023

Study finds slightly higher risk of autism diagnosis in areas with more lithium in drinking water, but experts say more research is needed

Tanggal: 03 Apr 2023 | Sumber: https://www.cnn.com/2023/04/03/health/autism-lithium-study/index.html

A new study found a moderately higher risk of autism spectrum disorder in children born to pregnant people exposed to tap water with higher levels of lithium, but experts caution that this association does not show a direct link between the two.

About 1 in 36 children in the US is diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) each year, according to data from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, scientists still don’t know the exact cause of autism, a developmental disorder. Genetics may be a factor, but some have been looking at potential environmental causes, too.

Autism diagnosis has become more common, but pandemic disrupted early detection, CDC says.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, cases may be on the rise, but that is also unclear. One study published this year on cases in the New York-New Jersey area found that autism diagnosis rates tripled among certain age groups between 2000 and 2016. A 2021 report found similar increases in cases, but the CDC says the increased number of cases is most likely linked to more doctors screening for the condition.

Berdasarkan laporan, lithium is an alkali metal that can be found naturally in some food and ground water. It’s used in batteries, grease and air conditioners, as well as in the treatment of bipolar disorder and some blood disorders. Its levels in US drinking water are not regulated, according to the US Geological Survey.

A new study, published Monday in the journal JAMA Pediatrics, found a small association between lithium and autism diagnosis in Denmark, where the researchers say the level of lithium in drinking water is similar to that in American water systems.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the researchers checked a database of people with psychiatric disorders for children born between 2000 and 2013 to find information on 8,842 cases of asd and 43,864 participants who did not have asd. They then measured the concentration of lithium in 151 public waterworks that served more than half of the Danish population and mapped out where pregnant people lived in relation.

For many neurodiverse people, 'The Sims' has been a lifelong comfort.

Berdasarkan laporan, as lithium levels in water increased, there was a modest increased risk of an asd diagnosis. Specifically, compared with people at the lowest exposure level, those who had the second and third highest exposure during pregnancy had a 24% to 26% higher risk of ASD diagnosed in children. The group with the highest exposure had a 46% higher risk than those at the lowest level of exposure.

The researchers could not tell how much water the pregnant people drank, but they picked Denmark in part because residents there consume some of the lowest amounts of bottled water in Europe.

Experts say it’s important to note that the research can’t show that lithium exposure leads directly to an autism diagnosis.

Berdasarkan laporan, further study is required, said study co-author dr. Beate Ritz, a professor of neurology in the David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA, and a professor of epidemiology and environmental health at the UCLA Fielding School of Public Health.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “any drinking water contaminants that may affect the developing human brain deserve intense scrutiny,” ritz said in a news release. She added that the research would need to be replicated in other countries to look for a similar connection.

Berdasarkan laporan, the implications of the findings are complex as far as public health policy is concerned, according to an editorial published alongside the study. Lithium levels in water, at concentrations that the study associated with a potential ASD risk, have also been linked with health benefits such as lower rates of hospitalization for psychiatric disorders and suicide.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “if all these of associations are valid, the wisdom of solomon will be required to develop guidelines for lithium in drinking water that are maximally protective of the entire population,” wrote dr. “Until the basic biology of ASD is better understood, it will be difficult to distinguish causal from spurious associations. David C. Bellinger, a professor of neurology and psychology at Harvard Medical School. ”.

'Heartbreaking' delays in autism diagnosis and treatment got even worse during pandemic.

Sebagaimana diketahui, dr. Max Wiznitzer, director of the Rainbow Autism Center at University Hospitals Rainbow Babies and Children’s Hospital in Cleveland, points to other research on the effects of lithium on pregnant people who take it for mental health disorders. Those studies – which look at people exposed to much higher levels than are found in drinking water – do not show a connection with autism spectrum disorder.

Diungkapkan bahwa “it’s an interesting association, but causation is definitely not proven,” said wiznitzer, who was not involved in the new research. “We have to see if there’s a viable and biologically plausible mechanism by which a small amount of lithium in the water supply can somehow do this, yet pharmacologic dosing of lithium in women with bipolar disorder has not been reported to be causing increased risk of ASD. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa other studies have also suggested connections between asd and environmental exposures to things like pesticides, air pollution and phthalates. But none of them points to any of these factors as a direct cause of the disorder.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, sign up here to get the results are in with dr. Sanjay Gupta every Tuesday from the CNN Health team.

Berdasarkan laporan, a link between environmental exposure and asd is hard to prove, wiznitzer said. With research showing that increased exposure to air pollution raises the risk of giving birth to a child with ASD, for example, he often wonders whether pollution is the determining factor or if it’s just the populations who live in more polluted areas.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “there’s a lot of speculation about about environmental factors, but how many of them are truly causally associated?” wiznitzer said. We have to figure out how to basically safely navigate them, and this is probably not one that’s high on our list. “We are bombarded with a variety of environmental stressors in our everyday lives. ”.

#264. Kwame Brathwaite, photographer of 'Black is Beautiful' movement, dies at 85

Tanggal: 04 Apr 2023 | Sumber: https://www.cnn.com/style/article/kwame-brathwaite-obituary-tan/index.html

Editor’s Note:  This article was originally published by The Art Newspaper, an editorial partner of CNN Style.

Kwame Brathwaite, the pioneering activist and photographer whose work helped define the aesthetics of the “Black is Beautiful” movement of the 1960s and beyond, died on April 1, aged 85.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, his son, kwame brathwaite, jr, announced his father’s death in an instagram post that read in part, “i am deeply saddened to share that my baba, the patriarch of our family, our rock and my hero has transitioned. ”.

Brathwaite’s work has been the subject of resurgent interest from curators, historians and collectors in recent years, and his first major institutional retrospective, which was organized by the Aperture Foundation, made its debut in 2019 at the Skirball Cultural Center in Los Angeles before touring the country.

Diungkapkan bahwa brathwaite was born in 1938 to barbadian immigrants, in what he referred to as “the people’s republic of brooklyn” in new york, though his family moved from there to harlem and then to the south bronx when brathwaite was 5 years old. The first was in August of 1955, when a 17-year-old Brathwaite encountered David Jackson’s haunting photograph of a brutalized Emmett Till in his open casket. He attended the School of Industrial Art (now the High School of Art and Design) and, according to profiles of Brathwaite in T Magazine and Vice, was drawn to photography by two moments. The second was in 1956, when — after he and his brother Elombe co-founded the African Jazz Arts Society and Studios (AJASS) — Brathwaite saw a young man taking photos in a dark jazz club without the use of a flash, and his mind became alight with possibility.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, using a hasselblad medium-format camera, brathwaite attempted to do the same, learning to work with limited light in a manner that enhanced the visual narrative of his imagery. He would soon also develop a darkroom technique that enriched and deepened how Black skin would appear in his photography, honing the practice in a small darkroom in his Harlem apartment. Brathwaite went on to photograph jazz legends performing throughout the 1950s and ’60s, including Miles Davis, John Coltrane, Thelonious Monk and others.

Berdasarkan laporan, “you want to get the feeling, the mood that you’re experiencing when they’re playing,” brathwaite told aperture magazine in 2017. “That’s the thing. You want to capture that. ”.

A 106-year-old from the Philippines is Vogue's oldest ever cover model.

Sebagaimana diketahui, by the early 1960s, alongside the rest of ajass, brathwaite began using his photography and organizing prowess to consciously push back against whitewashed, eurocentric beauty standards. In 1966, Brathwaite married his wife Sikolo, a Grandassa Model whom he had met on the street the year prior when he asked if he could take her portrait. In 1962, AJASS organized “Naturally ’62”, a fashion show held in a Harlem club called the Purple Manor and featuring the models. The show would go on to be held regularly until 1992. The group came up with the concept of the Grandassa Models, young Black women whom Brathwaite would photograph, celebrating and accentuating their features. The two remained married for the rest of Brathwaite’s life.

Diungkapkan bahwa by the 1970s, brathwaite’s focus on jazz shifted to other forms of popular black music. In 1974, he traveled to Africa with the Jackson Five to document their tour, also photographing the historic “Rumble in the Jungle” boxing match between Muhammad Ali and George Foreman in what’s now the Democratic Republic of Congo that same year. Commissions in this era also saw Brathwaite photographing Nina Simone, Stevie Wonder, Sly and the Family Stone, Bob Marley and other music legends.

Creating for community: The Black designers placing identity and heritage at the center of their brands.

Sebagaimana diketahui, throughout the ensuing decades, brathwaite continued to explore and develop his mode of photography, all through the lens of the “black is beautiful” ethos. In 2016, Brathwaite joined the roster of Philip Martin Gallery in Los Angeles, and he was continuing to photograph commissions as recently as 2018, when he shot artist and stylist Joanne Petit-Frère for The New Yorker.

Diungkapkan bahwa t magazine’s 2021 profile, published on the occasion of brathwaite’s retrospective traveling to the blanton museum of art in austin, texas, noted that the photographer’s health was failing such that he was unable to be interviewed for the article. A separate exhibition, “Kwame Brathwaite: Things Well Worth Waiting For,” is currently on view at the Art Institute of Chicago, where it will remain until July 24.

#268. This boiled bag of offal is banned in the US. In Scotland it's a fine-dining treat

📅 03 Apr 2023

This boiled bag of offal is banned in the US. In Scotland it's a fine-dining treat

Tanggal: 03 Apr 2023 | Sumber: https://www.cnn.com/travel/article/haggis-scotland-secrets/index.html

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, anthony bourdain loved haggis. But even the late, great American chef, writer and television host recognized that Scotland’s national dish, with its “sinister sheep parts” wrapped in a shroud of mystery and half-invented history, could be a hard sell.

Diungkapkan bahwa “don’t let them tell you otherwise, that’s really one of life’s great pleasures,” bourdain said on one of his gastro-curious pilgrimages to glasgow. “There is no more unfairly reviled food on Earth than the haggis. ”.

A mash-up of diced lung, liver and heart mixed with oatmeal, beef suet, onion and assorted spices, haggis was traditionally made by stuffing these raw ingredients into the stomach of a recently slain sheep and boiling the lot to a state of palatability.

Diungkapkan bahwa instagrammable is not the word that immediately comes to mind. In our 21st-century world, where “clean” eating and processed pap overlap, haggis can seem like an “Outlander”-style outlier from another age.

Sebagaimana diketahui, yet, by some alchemy, once cooked to its required “warm-reekin’ (steaming)” state, it adds up to much more than the sum of its modest parts. It’s offaly charm has kept nose-to-tail eating alive among a younger generation of Scots that has largely turned its back on the tripe, liver and kidneys their predecessors enjoyed (or endured).

Carefully prepared, haggis tastes both oaty and meaty; it is dark and crumbly, a little crispy at the edges but still moist; earthy but also savory and spicy; deep-tasting and profoundly warming, the perfect foil for its traditional garnish of floury mashed potatoes and orange bashed turnip.

“It’s like a cuddle for the stomach,” says Nicola Turner, a 35-year-old office administrator from Helensburgh, a town on western Scotland’s Firth of Clyde.

For children of the 1960s and ’70s, like crime novelist Ian Rankin, haggis meals were a choice between the classic meat-and-two-veg plate and the battered and deep-fried, chip-shop iteration loved by both his friend Bourdain and his quintessentially Scottish detective character, Inspector John Rebus.

Now myriad other treatments have blossomed.

Diungkapkan bahwa “i’m pretty sure the first time i dined with ab in edinburgh we had haggis in filo pastry with a jam-style – maybe blackcurrant – sauce,” rankin recalled. “He was a big fan of haggis and of chip shops. Rebus will have enjoyed the occasional haggis supper from his local chip shop. He was definitely a fan, as am I. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “it is all about the spicing and the texture,” says the scottish food writer, novelist and cook sue lawrence, a champion of haggis’ adaptability for use in other dishes. ’ It is all nicely chopped up and the oatmeal gives it a lovely texture. “If you didn’t know what was in it, you wouldn’t think ‘oh that tastes of liver or whatever. It could easily be a nice, big mince dish. ”.

These US restaurants and chefs are James Beard Award finalists.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, lawrence uses haggis as an alternative to beef and pork ragù in lasagna and in her pastilla, a version of the north african dish in which a hand-made haggis from the isle of mull substitutes for the traditional poultry or seafood filling. The filo pastry savory is flavored with the spice blend ras el hanout, apricots, chile, orange zest and almonds before being sprinkled with cinnamon and icing sugar.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, such cultural crossovers serve as a reminder that haggis could easily be a dish with nothing specifically scottish about it at all. Records of similar quick and portable preparations of the fast-perishing innards of sheep and other animals date back to ancient Rome and Greece.

Berdasarkan laporan, haggis-like combinations of offal and grains are part of the culinary history of several countries. Spain has chireta, Romania drob and Sweden polsa, while chaudin, or ponce, is a rice and meat-stuffed pig stomach that is a staple of Cajun cooking.

In neighboring England, recipes for “hagese,” “hagws of a schepe,” “haggas” or “haggus” pop up in recipe books published between the 15th and 17th centuries, probably preceding written records north of the border.

Etymological evidence points to the term “haggis” having its roots in Old Norse, suggesting an early version of an oat-and-offal sausage might have arrived in Britain and Ireland on a Viking longboat.

But ever since it was first optioned by the poet Robert Burns in the late 1700s, the haggis backstory has been monopolized by Scotland and the Scots, sometimes mischievously.

It is, according to the kind of lore that Burns engendered, the dish a doughty Highlander would carry with him as he drove cattle through the glens to the markets of the central belt or the perfect picnic for a whisky smuggler plying his illicit trade by moonlight.

Berdasarkan laporan, from such romantic notions it was a short step to turning the haggis into a wee wild beastie, one with longer legs on one side that was thus condemned to run round and round whichever hill it lived on. In 2003, a poll of American tourists in Scotland found that one in three of them believed they might encounter such a confused creature on a Caledonian vacation.

Sebagaimana diketahui, bourdain, a native new yorker, may have qualified as haggis’ biggest admirer since burns, but his compatriots at the us department of agriculture remain unconverted to offal-filled paunch. Haggis imports into the United States were prohibited in 1971 as part of a ban on the consumption of all livestock lungs. Authentic versions of old school haggis remain culinary contraband in the US, as hard to lay your hands on as Cuban cigars.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, across the rest of the world, it’s a different story. According to leading producer Simon Howie, haggis is more widely appreciated and consumed now than it has been since Burns improvised his “Address to a Haggis” for the entertainment of well-to-do Edinburgh acquaintances.

Firmly tongue-in-cheek, the poem lauds the “Great chieftain o’ the pudding race,” as exactly the kind of unpretentious, hearty fare required to nourish a nation of braveheart warriors.

In comparison to the enfeebling foreign muck enjoyed by the capital’s claret-quaffing elites of the time – the olio, fricassée or ragoût that would “sicken a sow” – Burns urges his readers to wonder at the magical impact of haggis on his fellow sons of Scotland’s soil.

As the English translation of the original Scots language version puts it:.

These days synthetic casings have largely replaced stomach but ovine and porcine innards remain at the core of most of the haggis produced in its homeland, said Howie, who estimates that his company Simon Howie Butchers, accounts for around 60% of the roughly two million haggises produced every year.

Diungkapkan bahwa for howie, versatility, value for money and convenience explain why this staple of the scottish larder is thriving. Typically haggis retails in Scotland, which accounts for half of global consumption by volume, for around £6, or $7. 70 per kilogram ($3. 36/pound). That’s around half the price of less expensive cuts of beef or a third of the price of Scotch lamb while enjoying a fairly similar nutritional and calorific profile.

“You can give your kids a meal that is not full of things you don’t want to feed them – for a few pounds you can feed three strapping lads,” Howie said.

Berdasarkan laporan, “from a kitchen perspective, it is very simple because when it leaves our factory it is already cooked. So when you or a restaurant owner gets it into the kitchen all you have to do is heat it up to be piping hot. It couldn’t be more basic: a student with no cooking skills or a Michelin-starred chef do exactly the same thing to put it out on the plate. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, its texture means haggis can also be usefully deployed in fine dining alongside leaner meat like venison or as a stuffing for poultry and game birds. Its spicy intensity means it is also finding uses in canapés and as a crouton-borne garnish for soups.

Buoyant sales are also underpinned by the increasing consumption of haggis in forms inspired by Scotland’s ethnic minorities.

Glasgow’s Sikh community pioneered haggis pakora in the 1990s and samosas, spring rolls and quesadillas have followed in its wake, often using a vegetarian version of the protein in which the offal is replaced by a mix of vegetables, pulses and mushrooms.

Berdasarkan laporan, such dishes are more than culinary twists. They are badges of belonging, and an indication that, two centuries after Burns grabbed it for the nation, haggis is as intimately entwined with Scots identity as ever.

Just ask Ross O’Cinneide, a promising 14-year-old fly-half in the junior section of Stirling County rugby club.

Diungkapkan bahwa “most of my friends and i like haggis,” he says. “Mum makes it for us sometimes after rugby and it’s got a very nice warming feeling. And it’s nice because it’s purely Scottish. ”.

#271. Musk's Twitter promised a purge of blue check marks. Instead he singled out the New York Times

Musk's Twitter promised a purge of blue check marks. Instead he singled out the New York Times

Tanggal: 03 Apr 2023 | Sumber: https://www.cnn.com/2023/04/03/tech/twitter-blue-checks/index.html

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, some vip twitter users woke up on saturday expecting to have lost their coveted blue verification check marks in a previously announced purge by elon musk. Instead, Twitter appeared to target a single account from a major publication Musk dislikes and changed the language on its site in a way that obscures why users are verified.

Diungkapkan bahwa twitter had said it would “begin winding down” blue checks granted under its old verification system — which emphasized protecting high-profile users at risk of impersonation — on april 1. In order to stay verified, Musk said, users would have to pay $8 per month to join the platform’s Twitter Blue subscription service, which has allowed accounts to pay for verification since December.

But one high-profile account did lose its blue check over the weekend: the main account for the New York Times, which had previously told CNN it would not pay for verification.

Diungkapkan bahwa william shatner is mad he may have to pay to keep his blue twitter checkmark. Elon Musk says too bad.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, after an account that often engages with musk posted a meme this weekend about the times declining to pay for verification, musk responded in a tweet saying, “oh ok, we’ll take it off then. ” Musk then lashed out at the Times — just the latest instance of the billionaire slamming journalists or media outlets — in a series of tweets that claimed the outlet’s coverage is boring and “propaganda. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, the weekend moves are just the latest example of twitter creating confusion and whiplash for users over feature changes — and in this case, not just any users, but many of the most high-profile accounts that have long been a key selling point for the platform. It also highlights how Musk often appears to guide decisions about the platform more by whims than by policy.

Berdasarkan laporan, although the new york times’ main account lost its blue check, its other accounts, such as those for its arts, travel and books content, remained verified. (It’s not clear why the New York Times doesn’t have a gold “organizations” check mark, like accounts for other news outlets, including the Associated Press and the Washington Post. ) After its blue check was removed, a spokesperson for the New York Times reiterated to CNN that it does not plan to pay for verification.

Twitter, which laid off most of its public relations staff last fall, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Berdasarkan laporan, in a separate puzzling move, twitter’s blue bird logo at the top of the site was replaced on monday with doge, the meme representing the cryptocurrency dogecoin, which musk has promoted. The price of dogecoin shot up 20% on Monday.

Musk has been threatening to take away “legacy” blue check marks from users verified under Twitter’s old system since shortly after he bought Twitter last fall.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in early november, twitter launched the option for people paying for its twitter blue subscription service to receive blue checks. The program was quickly put on pause after being plagued by a wave of celebrity and corporate impersonators, and was relaunched in December.

Twitter also rolled out a color-coded verification system with differently colored marks for companies and government entities, but Musk continued to say that individual users would eventually have to pay for blue checks.

In the days leading up to the blue check purge that wasn’t, prominent users such as actor William Shatner and anti-bullying activist Monica Lewinksy pushed back against the idea that, as power users that draw attention to the site, they should have to pay for a feature that keeps them safe from impersonation.

Berdasarkan laporan, by muddying the reason accounts are verified, the new label could risk making it easier for people to scam or impersonate high-profile users. Diungkapkan bahwa chelsea has spent over $600 million on new signings. Here's why that's significant.

But, on Sunday, the club announced that it had sacked its manager after an underwhelming spell in charge.

Potter managed to win just 10 of the 28 league matches this season and leaves the team 11th in the Premier League table.

In recent weeks, players had looked a shadow of their former selves and many fans had lost confidence that Potter’s plan for the club could ever work.

“On behalf of everyone at the club, we want to thank Graham sincerely for his contribution to Chelsea,” the club’s co-owners Todd Boehly and Behdad Eghbali said in a statement.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we have the highest degree of respect for graham as a coach and as a person. He has always conducted himself with professionalism and integrity and we are all disappointed in this outcome. ”.

The club was punching above its weight financially and, as a result, carefully selected new signings which would compliment Potter’s style of play.

The approach paid off as the team became an established Premier League outfit which has gone on to greater things this season – the Seagulls currently sit sixth in the league and in the UEFA Conference League qualification spot.

At Chelsea, it seemed the complete opposite.

As was the case under previous owner Roman Abramovich, the club expected instant results and used its financial weight to sign a number of high-profile names, including the likes of Enzo Fernández and Mykhailo Mudryk.

Despite his impressive CV, Potter had never managed superstars and suddenly found himself in a changing room with multiple.

The scatter gun approach to recruitment also left the team lacking balance and organization with Potter failing to get a tune out of a team busting with talent.

In truth, many had raised an eyebrow when Potter, inexperienced at the very top level, was chosen to replace Thomas Tuchel as manager.

Despite falling out of favor with fans by the end of his tenure, Tuchel had guided Chelsea to the Champions League title in 2021 and is still considered by many as one of the best coaches in the world.

The German has gone on to sign with Bavarian giant Bayern Munich through the 2024/25 season and recently told reporters he needed “quite a bit of time to distance himself from Chelsea” because leaving the club had hurt him.

Bayern Munich sacks manager Julian Nagelsmann, appoints Thomas Tuchel.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i feel for graham potter, but it was inevitable. Ridiculous decision to start with. You don’t change Tuchel for Potter. ”.

With 10 games left in the league and a Champions League quarterfinal against Real Madrid on the horizon, Chelsea still has plenty to play for.

Assistant coach Bruno Saltor will take over on an interim basis, but Boehly and his team must now look for a long-term replacement capable – and willing – to bring order to Chelsea’s chaos.

Potter’s sacking is yet another sign of just how transient managers can be in the top-flight of English football, especially when results aren’t instantaneous.

There has now been a record 12 sackings in the Premier League so far this season, with Potter leaving his position the same day Leicester boss Brendan Rodgers was sacked from his.

The previous record was 10 manager changes in a single season, set in four other campaigns, most recently in 2017/18.

Y’all didn’t have any issues with it at all. We’re not doing double standards here. So don’t be all outraged and talking about class and sportsmanship when Angel Reese does the same thing. ”.

#295. The haunting Masters meltdown that changed Rory McIlroy's career

📅 03 Apr 2023

The haunting Masters meltdown that changed Rory McIlroy's career

Tanggal: 03 Apr 2023 | Sumber: https://www.cnn.com/2023/04/03/golf/rory-mcilroy-masters-meltdown-2011-spt-spc-intl/index.html

Editor’s Note:  This story was originally published in April 2023.

Slumped on his club, head buried in his arm, Rory McIlroy looked on the verge of tears.

The then-21-year-old had just watched his ball sink into the waters of Rae’s Creek at Augusta National and with it, his dream of winning The Masters, a dream that had looked so tantalizingly close mere hours earlier.

As a four-time major winner and one of the most decorated names in the sport’s history, few players would turn down the chance to swap places with McIlroy heading into Augusta this week.

Yet on Sunday afternoon of April 10, 2011, not a golfer in the world would have wished to be in the Northern Irishman’s shoes.

A fresh-faced, mop-headed McIlroy had touched down in Georgia for the first major of the season with a reputation as the leading light of the next generation of stars.

An excellent 2010 had marked his best season since turning pro three years earlier, highlighted by a first PGA Tour win at the Quail Hollow Championship and a crucial contribution to Team Europe’s triumph at the Ryder Cup.

Yet despite a pair of impressive top-three finishes at the Open and PGA Championship respectively, a disappointing missed cut at The Masters – his first at a major – served as ominous foreshadowing.

McIlroy shot 74 and 77 to fall four strokes short of the cut line at seven-over par, a performance that concerned him enough to take a brief sabbatical from competition.

But one year on in 2011, any lingering Masters demons looked to have been exorcised as McIlroy flew round the Augusta fairways.

Having opened with a bogey-free seven-under 65 – the first time he had ever shot in the 60s at the major – McIlroy pulled ahead from Spanish first round co-leader Alvaro Quirós with a second round 69.

It sent him into the weekend holding a two-shot cushion over Australia’s Jason Day, with Tiger Woods a further stroke behind and back in the hunt for a 15th major after a surging second round 66.

Diungkapkan bahwa and yet the 21-year-old leader looked perfectly at ease with having a target on his back. Even after a tentative start to the third round, McIlroy rallied with three birdies across the closing six holes to stretch his lead to four strokes heading into Sunday.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the youngster was out on his own ahead of a bunched chasing pack comprising day, ángel cabrera, k. Choi and Charl Schwartzel. J. After 54 holes, McIlroy had shot just three bogeys.

“It’s a great position to be in … I’m finally feeling comfortable on this golf course,” McIlroy told reporters.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i’m not getting ahead of myself, i know how leads can dwindle away very quickly. I have to go out there, not take anything for granted and go out and play as hard as I’ve played the last three days. If I can do that, hopefully things will go my way.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we’ll see what happens tomorrow because four shots on this golf course isn’t that much. ”.

The truth can hurt, and McIlroy was about to prove his assessment of Augusta to be true in the most excruciating way imaginable.

Berdasarkan laporan, his fourth bogey of the week arrived immediately. Having admitted to expecting some nerves at the first tee, McIlroy sparked a booming opening drive down the fairway, only to miss his putt from five feet.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, three consecutive pars steadied the ship, but schwartzel had the wind in his sails. A blistering birdie, par, eagle start had seen him draw level at the summit after his third hole.

A subsequent bogey from the South African slowed his charge, as McIlroy clung onto a one-shot lead at the turn from Schwartzel, Cabrera, Choi, and a rampaging Woods, who shot five birdies and an eagle across the front nine to send Augusta into a frenzy.

Despite his dwindling advantage and the raucous Tiger-mania din ahead of him, McIlroy had responded well to another bogey at the 5th hole, draining a brilliant 20-foot putt at the 7th to restore his lead.

The fist pump that followed marked the high-water point of McIlroy’s round, as a sliding start accelerated into full-blown free-fall at the par-four 10th hole.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, his tee shot went careening into a tree, ricocheting to settle between the white cabins that separate the main course from the adjacent par-three course. It offered viewers a glimpse at a part of Augusta rarely seen on broadcast, followed by pictures of McIlroy anxiously peering out from behind a tree to track his follow-up shot.

Diungkapkan bahwa though his initial escape was successful, yet another collision with a tree and a two-putt on the green saw a stunned mcilroy eventually tap in for a triple bogey. Having led the field one hole and seven shots earlier, he arrived at the 11th tee in seventh.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, by the time his tee drive at the 13th plopped into the creek, all thoughts of who might be the recipient of the green jacket had long-since switched away from the anguished youngster. It had taken him seven putts to navigate the previous two greens, as a bogey and a double bogey dropped him to five-under – the score he had held after just 11 holes of the tournament.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mercifully, the last five holes passed without major incident. A missed putt for birdie from five feet at the final hole summed up McIlroy’s day, though he was given a rousing reception as he left the green.

Berdasarkan laporan, mere minutes earlier, the same crowd had erupted as schwartzel sunk his fourth consecutive birdie to seal his first major title. After starting the day four shots adrift of McIlroy, the South African finished 10 shots ahead of him, and two ahead of second-placed Australian duo Jason Day and Adam Scott.

Sebagaimana diketahui, mcilroy’s eight-over 80 marked the highest score of the round. Having headlined the leaderboard for most of the week, he finished tied-15th.

Tears would flow during a phone call with his parents the following morning, but at his press conference, McIlroy was upbeat.

“I’m very disappointed at the minute, and I’m sure I will be for the next few days, but I’ll get over it,” he said.

“I was leading this golf tournament with nine holes to go, and I just unraveled … It’s a Sunday at a major, what it can do.

Diungkapkan bahwa “this is my first experience at it, and hopefully the next time i’m in this position i’ll be able to handle it a little better. I didn’t handle it particularly well today obviously, but it was a character-building day … I’ll come out stronger for it. ”.

Once again, McIlroy would be proven right.

Berdasarkan laporan, just eight weeks later in june, mcilroy rampaged to an eight-shot victory at the us open. Records tumbled in his wake at Congressional, as he shot a tournament record 16-under 268 to become the youngest major winner since Tiger Woods at The Masters in 1997.

Berdasarkan laporan, the historic victory kickstarted a golden era for mcilroy. After coasting to another eight-shot win at the PGA Championship in 2012, McIlroy became only the third golfer since 1934 to win three majors by the age of 25 with triumph at the 2014 Open Championship.

Before the year was out, he would add his fourth major title with another PGA Championship win.

Berdasarkan laporan, and much of it was owed to that fateful afternoon at augusta. In an interview with the BBC in 2015, McIlroy dubbed it “the most important day” of his career.

“If I had not had the whole unravelling, if I had just made a couple of bogeys coming down the stretch and lost by one, I would not have learned as much.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “luckily, it did not take me long to get into a position like that again when i was leading a major and i was able to get over the line quite comfortably. It was a huge learning curve for me and I needed it, and thankfully I have been able to move on to bigger and better things.

Diungkapkan bahwa “looking back on what happened in 2011, it doesn’t seem as bad when you have four majors on your mantelpiece. ”.

McIlroy’s contentment came with a caveat: it would be “unthinkable” if he did not win The Masters in his career.

Yet as he prepares for his 15th appearance at Augusta National this week, a green jacket remains an elusive missing item from his wardrobe.

Despite seven top-10 finishes in his past 10 Masters outings, the trophy remains the only thing separating McIlroy from joining the ranks of golf immortals to have completed golf’s career grand slam of all four majors in the modern era: Gene Sarazen, Ben Hogan, Gary Player, Jack Nicklaus, and Tiger Woods.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a runner-up finish to scottie scheffler last year marked mcilroy’s best finish at augusta, yet arguably 2011 remains the closest he has ever been to victory. A slow start in 2022 meant McIlroy had begun Sunday’s deciding round 10 shots adrift of the American, who teed off for his final hole with a five-shot lead despite McIlroy’s brilliant 64 finish.

Berdasarkan laporan, at 33 years old, time is still on his side. Though 2022 extended his major drought to eight years, it featured arguably his best golf since that golden season in 2014.

And as McIlroy knows better than most, things can change quickly at Augusta National.

Jordan Hawkins, who scored 16 points for UConn, talked about winning the crown one day after his cousin, Angel Reese of Louisiana State University, won the women’s title.

“I mean it’s absolutely amazing that we both get this opportunity and I mean the family reunion is going to be great so that’s all I know,” he said.

Berdasarkan laporan, uconn enters rarefied air as only the sixth team to win five ncaa men’s basketball championships, joining ucla (11), kentucky (eight), north carolina (six), duke (five) and indiana (five). All of UConn’s titles have come since 1999 with the most recent before Monday occurring in 2014.

UConn’s women’s teams have won 11 basketball national titles.

CNN’s Steve Almasy and Issy Ronald contributed to this report.

Diungkapkan bahwa “i believe in an all-inclusive country music. Twain, who was presented the award by rapper Megan Thee Stallion, shouted out some of the diverse acts she is spotlighting on her “Queen of Me” tour this year, including Lily Rose, Lindsay Ell, Hailey Whitters, Mickey Guyton and others.

#366. What’s behind Australia’s surge in teen extremism?

📅 13 Nov 2026

What’s behind Australia’s surge in teen extremism?

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/nov/13/australia-surge-in-teen-extremism-ntwnfb

Young people are being found with ‘hard drives full of what can only be described as gore’, one expert says.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

In March, Guardian Australia revealed that most people who have been charged with the new federal crime of possession of violent extremist material are under 18.

This week Australian federal police sounded the alarm about a surge in teen extremism: 32 of the 37 young people prosecuted in counter-terrorism cases since 2020 were charged in the past two years.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the growth in youth extremism is happening within a sprawling online ecosystem. My investigations have tracked the rise of online networks that urge violence and nihilism for their own sake, in which perpetrators coerce victims not much younger than themselves to commit brutal and degrading acts.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in a review of 55 youth terrorism cases, the afp has found that the profile is mixed. They are often young men. Many have received some support or intervention for a mental health condition. Some are from stable homes, others not.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, what they have most in common is that they are young people on the internet. Experts say the age of those caught up in these crimes is decreasing.

In the last month two teenagers in Darwin have been charged with collecting documents that could facilitate acts of terrorism.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the arrests came five months after another nt teenager was charged with making posts with “pro-nazi, anti-immigration, anti-trans and white nationalist themes”. The charge sheet alleges he also possessed videos of white nationalist terrorist attacks, including the 2019 Christchurch mosque shooting and the 2022 Buffalo shooting that it partly inspired.

Experts involved in harm prevention programs, including the Victoria University professor Debra Smith, have watched the age of this cohort decrease dramatically over the past decade.

Instead of considering the challenge exclusively through the lens of radicalisation, Smith says we need to recognise that some young people are being socialised and finding identity in online spaces that may appear exciting and transgressive but are ultimately harmful to themselves, and may encourage them to do harm to others.

She has seen cases where teenagers are being found with “hard drives full of what can only be described as gore”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “it’s like getting involved in any other … unhealthy subcultural aspect of life … [such as] gangs or crime for payment,” she says. “There’s this offering of what young people can look at and get involved in that just simply wasn’t there years ago. ”.

The Guardian’s investigation into the growth of extremist material charges, as well as the surge of young people in Australia ensnared in sadistic online extortion and gore networks, reveals an amorphous online ecosystem in which young people may easily come into contact with extreme and violent content.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a teenager in new south wales who pleaded guilty to possessing violent extremist material, among other charges, described how he first came across such content on tiktok when he was 14 and sought validation by talking to others online. He used ChatGPT to research the Boston marathon bomber Dzhokhar Tsarnaev as well as security arrangements at the Sydney Opera House. He was sentenced to a three-year community corrections order.

Others have told police how they became involved in so-called “gore” channels on Telegram, where more and more extreme footage – including of animal abuse – is traded.

Given the age of many involved, Levi West, a research fellow at the Australian National University, says they may be considered as much victims as perpetrators, which is a significant challenge for how authorities respond.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it’s important for parents, schools and others to think about what’s sitting underneath the uptick in numbers, he says, and not just the “algorithms”. He points to the legacies of Covid-19 and lockdowns as well as the presence of screens and digital technologies in the lives of young people.

“We are not going to arrest our way out of this problem,” West says.

With people as young as 13 before the courts, Australia must consider if authorities are taking the right approach and have the right resources for this challenge.

The Guardian’s investigation into the possession of extremist material charges in South Australia and around the country found that many of those who had been before the courts faced a range of health and social difficulties, including autism diagnoses and learning challenges – and raised questions about whether some young people understand a crime has been committed.

Smith has seen many young people caught up in these activities who come from troubled family backgrounds, while others have had every opportunity in life.

There is a role for everyone involved in caring for young people, she says, from parents and schools to sporting clubs, to recognise when someone might be engaging in harmful behaviours long before there is a risk of violence, then help them access non-punitive pathways for help.

“It’s really important to understand it through a developmental lens – that these are young people who are making decisions with young brains,” Smith says.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “my grave concern is that if we are just giving everyone terrorism offences at [age] 12, 13, 14, 15, we’re starting to label them the thing that they will become. ”.

A former NSW Liberal politician is facing the possibility of a significant jail term after a jury found him guilty of raping a 13-year-old boy.

The former MP Rory Amon was found guilty by a jury, after about four hours of deliberation on Friday, of one count of sexual intercourse with a person aged between 10 and 14 and indecently assaulting a child.

The 37-year-old was facing his second NSW supreme court trial after a different jury acquitted him in March on eight separate charges of child sexual offending, but could not reach a verdict on the two counts decided on Friday.

The charges related to Amon’s interactions with a 13-year-old boy who the former MP met on an adults-only website, the court heard.

Amon always maintained his innocence, saying he held an honest and reasonable belief that the boy was over the age of 16.

The original trial was told the boy inflated his age when signing up to the gay hook-up app, and again while talking with Amon.

Amon and the boy exchanged explicit images before a 2017 meeting in the carpark of the boy’s apartment block, the court heard.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, at the time he first contacted the youth, amon was working full-time for the federal mp for mackellar, jason falinski. Amon went on to serve two terms on Northern Beaches council before being elected as the Liberal MP for the state seat of Pittwater in 2023.

The charges scuppered Amon’s fledgling career in state politics, forcing his expulsion from the Liberal party and his resignation after his election in March 2023.

His exit had implications for the state Liberals, which lost the formerly safe seat to a teal independent at the subsequent byelection.

Amon remains on bail and will return to court for a sentencing hearing on 27 November.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he is the third former nsw mp convicted of sexual offences in recent years. The former Kiama MP and Coalition minister Gareth Ward was jailed in 2025 for the sexual abuse of two young men, including a political staffer who was intoxicated after an event at NSW Parliament House. His three-year-nine-month minimum term expires in April 2029.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the former nsw minister milton orkopoulos was found guilty in 2023 of sexually abusing teenage boys while he was a state labor mp. A jury found the 65-year-old guilty of 26 charges of sexual offending against four underage boys and supplying them with drugs over a decade, ending in 2003.

He had already served more than a decade in prison for sexual assault of a minor, indecent assault, supplying heroin and cannabis and other offences.

When the outbreak was first detected in May, it resembled a single, giant blaze, with infections concentrated in a handful of towns in one province.

Microsoft 365 Services, including Teams, Outlook and Microsoft's artificial intelligence software Copilot, have been affected by "connectivity problems".

Customers are reporting varying levels of access - many have not been able to send or receive emails, view certain files or details on their calendar apps.

Some users have been able to use Teams and are using messaging and online meeting functions without issues.

More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps according to Microsoft's website.

The full scale of the outage has not been confirmed, but monitoring website Downdetector had 140,000 people from 74 countries report issues with Outlook on Thursday evening.

The real figure affected is likely much higher because Downdetector relies primarily on users self-reporting.

Microsoft 365 is also used by companies worldwide and is expected to have a knock-on effect to other services.

Tech giants OpenAI and Anthropic have both reported problems as a result of the outage.

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said it was investigating an issue affecting its connections to Microsoft's services, which has caused some tools to not work as expected.

From city governments in the US to Australian spy agencies, disruption across the globe has been widespread.

Courts from Los Angeles to Texas warned that communications might be delayed.

In Canada, the public broadcaster CBC reported that a healthcare network running several hospitals in Toronto was experiencing email issues, but that patient care was not affected.

The government of Japan also said its shared IT platform had been disrupted.

Across the UK, GP surgeries, pharmacies, police and schools have been affected by the outage.

Some GP surgeries have urged patients not to submit messages via their website while the problem remains, while several large police forces are urging members of the public to call if they want to make a report.

Microsoft has ruled out a cyber-attack and attributed the ongoing outage to "elevated load" on its infrastructure.

The term refers to when servers are handling a much higher volume of stress than they usually do.

In the case of the Microsoft outage, a large number of servers became "unexpectedly unavailable", the company said, which sent added traffic to remaining servers, straining these.

On Friday afternoon, Microsoft said it had seen "encouraging recovery progress" in Europe and improvement in North America.

The company added it is focused on "addressing the remaining areas of disruption" and warned "some users may still experience intermittent issues as recovery actions continue".

In an earlier statement, the tech giant had said that its attempted fixes were "not taking as expected".

Although email service Outlook appears to be resuming for some, the outage has so far lasted for more than 20 hours - in outage terms that is considered a long time.

Prof James Ferryman from the University of Reading's department of computer science said the details the company has disclosed provide some clues.

"What Microsoft has told us is that the part of its servers that sets up secure connections is getting swamped, and once that happens the server just stops answering," he said.

"The trouble is that this kind of failure snowballs.

"One server falls over, its work gets passed to the next one, and meanwhile huge numbers of phones and laptops keep trying to get back in.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "you can't just turn it all back on at once. You have to bring it back bit by bit. ".

The challenge is therefore not just fixing the fault, but managing the huge surge of devices trying to reconnect once services start coming back online.

Gergely Orosz, a former leading software engineer at several major tech companies including Skype and Uber, said this could be the "most disruptive" business email outage "of all time".

He said it was still difficult to know just how many people have been affected by the disruption, but added he "cannot recall" an outage over business email ever taking this long to return to normal.

Australian cyber-security expert Troy Hunt told the BBC the outage could have far-reaching consequences.

"Microsoft is a massive part of the internet backbone and reminds us how critical email still is.

"Not only does this outage affect many people's ability to work but also things like the ability to communicate about appointments, purchase things that need verification, create or access accounts and services," he said.

#373. Study Hard, Get a Career and Get Ahead? It’s Not What It Used to Be.

📅 13 Nov 2026

Study Hard, Get a Career and Get Ahead? It’s Not What It Used to Be.

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/13/world/europe/education-meritocracy.html

From India to France, the implicit meritocratic bargain that underwrote stable societies by providing advancement to new generations is breaking down.

Diungkapkan bahwa protest movements have long relied on students as some of the most ardent foot soldiers. Young people have been on the front lines of protests against war, climate change and racial inequality. But in huge protests that have shaken India and France this fall, students have revolted against the failed promises of education itself.

Diungkapkan bahwa in india, students took to the streets after the government abruptly canceled the results of a medical-school admissions exam because test questions had been leaked online. Aspiring doctors had to take the test again, after many spent years studying for up to 12 hours a day in hopes of winning one of the coveted spots — and the chance of upward mobility. Young people across the country saw the scandal as emblematic of a broken education system and were furious.

Diungkapkan bahwa in france, students in poor suburbs outside paris began protesting the decrepit physical condition of their schools, an opaque university admissions system and absent teachers. French education had long promised to serve as a “social elevator” enabling young people to advance in society, but had fallen into disrepair. Soon, demonstrations spread across the country and, in some cities, spiraled into rioting.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in both countries, the anger of the students shows no signs of abating. And while in many ways France and India could hardly be more different, their unrest was sparked by a similar source of outrage: the breakdown of a foundational social contract that one could call the meritocratic bargain.

Berdasarkan laporan, it is a promise that lies at the core of many countries’ political compacts. Educational achievements are a good measure of merit because education is open to all and leads to valuable skills. Though specifics can vary, the central proposition usually goes something like this: A fair society rewards merit. Therefore, education should be a route to social and economic advancement.

Diungkapkan bahwa the value of this system is not just that it selects for those with high ability, but also that it offers a justification for the resulting socioeconomic hierarchy — including who ends up at the bottom. “All selection mechanisms generate losers,” said Nicholas Kuipers, a professor at Princeton University who studies the politics of meritocracy. “The question is, Who do you want to be a loser, and who do you want to be a winner?”.

Diungkapkan bahwa a bird that flies south from its breeding grounds in siberia to winter in south and south-east asia has been found thousands of miles off course in cumbria. Regrettably, it was found by a cat.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, chris hind, cumbria’s county recorder for birds, said it was “extraordinary” that a siberian rubythroat was found on his patch, albeit dead. There have been only 17 recorded instances of the bird in the UK, 15 of those in the northern Scottish isles.

Diungkapkan bahwa hind was contacted by the rspb at the weekend after a womanwho lives in a remote north cumbrian valley reported the bird. She had recognised it was out of the ordinary and put the dead bird in her freezer.

Diungkapkan bahwa “she realised that it was something unusual,” hind said. “She probably didn’t realise how incredibly unusual it is. There are only two accepted records of it from mainland Britain. ”.

The woman, who wants to remain anonymous, told the BBC she had “heard the cat flap go” and her heart sank when her cat “brought her a bird and trotted off”.

“I saw the bird’s distinctive, beautiful orange-red feather patch under its beak but I couldn’t recognise the species,” she said.

Quite why the bird appears to have headed west, rather than south, is a mystery although Hind pointed to the puzzle of yellow-browed warblers that have been spotted in the UK in increasing numbers in recent decades.

“It used to be thought that these are birds which had just got lost but there are academics now thinking that it may be something rather more purposeful,” he said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, hind said the bird brought in by the cat was very underweight, weighing 28 grams (just under 1oz). Textbooks say it should be about 73 grams.

Diungkapkan bahwa siberian rubythroats were also extremely secretive, he said. “They tend to creep around in the vegetation and the place where it was found was a place hugely vegetated, lots of trees, lots of bushes, lots of hedges in a remote little valley. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the plan is now for academics to take samples and then the bird – currently in hind’s freezer – will go to tullie house museum in carlisle. The nuclear agency has not been able to inspect any sites attacked by the US and Israel last year.

The UN's nuclear watchdog has said it is "increasingly concerned" about a nuclear facility in Iran which it has not been allowed to inspect.

Berdasarkan laporan, iran informed the international atomic energy agency (iaea) of plans to set up the uranium enrichment plant in the city of isfahan a day before israel began attacking its nuclear sites last june. The US joined the strikes later that month.

In a report seen by news agencies, the IAEA said it does not know the exact location or whether it contains nuclear material.

Since the start of the latest war, Iran has restricted IAEA inspectors' access to its nuclear sites, preventing the agency from verifying its enriched uranium stockpile.

Sebagaimana diketahui, under a 2015 nuclear deal, iran agreed to limit its enriched uranium stockpile to 300kg and enrichment to 3. 67% purity. It subsequently exceeded both.

Before the June 2025 strikes, it had accumulated an estimated 441kg enriched to 60%, close to weapons grade.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the nuclear complex at isfahan suffered extensive damage in us and israeli strikes, particularly the parts above the ground. The condition of its underground facilities is not clear.

The IAEA believes much of Iran's highly enriched uranium was stored there.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "the agency's lack of information about [iran's] nuclear material and access to facilities to verify it is a matter of serious proliferation concern. and needs to be rectified with the utmost urgency," it said in the latest report.

Iran announced plans for the Isfahan Fuel Enrichment Plant (IFEP) on 12 June 2025, shortly after an IAEA resolution which declared Iran had failed to meet its nuclear safeguards obligations.

Iran initially agreed to allow inspectors to visit the facility, but the inspection was cancelled after Israel launched attacks the following day.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the iaea's latest calls come almost a year after it made a similar appeal to iran. At the time it said it had only inspected some of the 13 nuclear facilities that were "unaffected" by the attacks and none of the seven that were.

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmvg2dvw0355o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

All parties have been banned at the university.

Four Nigerian students have died after attending a party in the south-eastern town of Nsukka to celebrate the end of their final exams.

The cause of death has not been confirmed but police spokesman Daniel Ndukwe said the two men and two women had reportedly fallen ill after consuming alcoholic drinks at the party.

The University of Nigeria Nsukka has declared three days of mourning, during which academic and social activities will be suspended.

The tragedy comes amid a wider crackdown on fake and adulterated alcoholic drinks in Nigeria, where the food and drug regulator has been raiding suspected producers of unsafe food and beverages.

The university's Vice-Chancellor, Professor Simon Ortuanya, said the university had received a distress call at 22:00 on Wednesday, and sent security personnel to a house party at Praise Lodge, outside the campus in Nsukka's Hilltop area.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "the preliminary investigation and interim report point to alleged alcohol abuse or drug paraphernalia and things like that. But we are not conclusive on those matters," he said.

He described the deaths as "tragic and painful".

"As a community, we mourn, not just alone, we mourn with the families, the parents that have suffered these years to train the men and women in their studies," he said.

Ortuanya also announced a ban on signing-out celebrations, which are commonly held by final-year students to mark the completion of their studies.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the celebrations often involve parties, dancing, photographs and friends signing one another's shirts. He urged students to use graduation as a time to reflect on their university experience and prepare for life beyond campus.

The university said it was working with security agencies to establish what had caused the deaths.

Diungkapkan bahwa the police have also launched an investigation. They said alcoholic drinks had been recovered from the scene and the bodies taken to a mortuary for autopsies.

The investigation comes amid wider concerns about unsafe alcoholic drinks in Nigeria.

In September, dozens of people fell ill after consuming locally made alcoholic drinks and herbal mixtures in communities across Ondo State, south-west Nigeria.

More than 11 people died in the Araromi-Obu area, while more than 50 others were hospitalised.

Investigations found that some of the drinks had been contaminated with methanol, a highly toxic form of alcohol that can cause blindness and death.

Diungkapkan bahwa nigeria's food and drug regulator, nafdac, reported more than 150 cases, including 48 confirmed deaths. More than 80 people were hospitalised, and five lost their sight.

The regulator has been carrying out raids across the country, targeting facilities suspected of producing fake or adulterated alcoholic drinks, food and beverages.

Nigeria has long struggled with the sale of unsafe and adulterated products, which campaigners warn pose a serious threat to public health.

Singer, 76, was in Manchester with his band for penultimate UK show of his Songs in the Key of Life anniversary tour.

When Stevie Wonder’s team just called to say: “Can we all come to your restaurant in Stalybridge at 11pm on a Sunday?” Ryan Robinson, of course, said yes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, first the band turned up, and then – at 12. 30am – the man himself arrived. Hours later, staff at the Cafe Continental were sharing a £1,000 tip.

It was, the co-owner admitted, “all a bit mad”, as he praised Wonder as someone who was happy to chat to everybody, and the team around him as down to earth and extremely polite.

Wonder, 76, was in Manchester with his band for the Sunday night gig at Co-op Live on his Songs in the Key of Life 50th anniversary tour.

It was the penultimate night of a 13-date European leg of the tour in which Wonder performed all 21 songs from his most celebrated album, which includes Have a Talk With God, Sir Duke, Joy Inside My Tears and Isn’t She Lovely.

Robinson told the Manchester Evening News that some of the musicians on the tour had already been in a few times, “as they often tour with other artists”.

“Every time they’ve visited, they’ve been like: ‘Stevie might come’, and we were always just thinking that it would be amazing but we never expected anything from it.

Berdasarkan laporan, “his band visited again on saturday and then we got the call to say they wanted to come again with stevie’s youngest daughter after their show in manchester, and they said again that stevie might come. We stayed open late for them, and then he turned up – it was all a bit mad!.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we normally just do a roast service on sunday, so it was a bit of a scramble to make it all happen and ensure we had the full menu ready for them, but everybody was so lovely. Stevie is actually a really nice guy and was happy to pose for photographs and have a chat. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, among the late-night diners was wonder’s daughter aisha, for whom he wrote isn’t she lovely when she was a newborn. You wouldn’t think they were these massive global superstars. Robinson said: “His daughter, his family, and his entire team are just all down to earth and very polite. I just kept looking over being like: ‘Is this actually happening?’ We’ve still not come to terms with it now!”.

Cafe Continental describes itself as a neighbourhood restaurant in the heart of Stalybridge, “offering a modern, day to night dining experience”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the superstar and his musicians dined on steak and seafood and before leaving they gave a £1,000 tip, which was shared among staff, robinson said. After the visit the restaurant posted on Facebook: “Surreal things happen now and again. This is one of them! Pleasure to welcome Mr Stevie Wonder to the restaurant to close off his tour!”.

Berdasarkan laporan, robinson said he thought the band had found the restaurant on social media. “But it’s brought them out here into the suburbs and it’s really nice to see. “If it wasn’t for social media, they more than likely may have Googled something nearby and it might have led them to the city centre,” he told the BBC. “It’s good for the area. For a small independent business like us to receive so much traction from this … getting a major celebrity to this town itself, it does a lot. ”.

#387. UK’s biggest insurer hit by rise in subsidence claims after record hot summer

UK’s biggest insurer hit by rise in subsidence claims after record hot summer

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/13/uk-insurer-rise-in-subsidence-claims-aviva-hastings-direct-axa

Increase reported by Aviva after Hastings Direct said claims were up 140% in August and Axa said it had been a ‘surge year’.

The UK’s largest insurer has been hit by a rise in subsidence claims after an extremely hot summer left households across the country grappling with the fallout from the growing climate crisis.

Aviva said on Friday it had experienced the jump amid an industry-wide surge in households filing subsidence claims with their insurers to cover repairs, which typically are needed to address cracks, sloping floors, and off-kilter doors and windows.

Berdasarkan laporan, it follows two record hot summers in the uk; august this year was the joint hottest month ever recorded around the world. Drier summers cause the ground under houses to shrink, which undermines a property’s foundations. It then expands in wetter winters, which can further damage homes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, aviva experienced a “peak subsidence period” between july and september, with claims continuing into october, its chief executive, amanda blanc, told bloomberg in an interview on friday. Aviva would not provide any further detail on the scale of the increase in claims.

Diungkapkan bahwa blanc said homeowners could reduce the risk of subsidence by keeping a close eye on drains, pipes and gutters, and fixing any leaks that could affect the ground under homes. “It’s about managing trees and plumbing,” she said.

Diungkapkan bahwa a number of fellow insurers have also experienced a rise in claims in recent months. Hastings Direct said it received record subsidence claims in August, up 140% compared with a year earlier. Axa, one of the UK’s biggest home insurers, has said it has been a “surge year” for subsidence.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the value of claims have also hit a record high. The average subsidence claim in the UK hit a high of £20,000 between April and June, more than £2,000 higher than a year earlier, according to the Association of British Insurers. Insurers paid out £72m for domestic subsidence claims, compared with £60m in the same period last year.

Berdasarkan laporan, millions of homes are at risk of subsidence because of the worsening climate crisis, according to the british geological survey, which estimates that up to 11% of uk homes – more than 4. 2m houses – could be at risk by 2070. Older properties with shallow foundations and those built on clay-rich soil are facing the biggest threat, with areas including London, Essex, Kent and areas around Oxford among the most vulnerable.
