Rosenberg: Uncompromising Putin ups demands for peace with Ukraine

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq39glwprknjo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Putin sounded uncompromising and confident at his talks with the US envoys.

Russia's President Vladimir Putin says he wishes "eternal peace" for Ukraine.

That is the same Russian president who ordered the full-scale invasion of Russia's neighbour nearly five years ago and who continues to reject the idea of a comprehensive ceasefire.

And what, in Moscow's view, is a prerequisite for peace?.

Diungkapkan bahwa the kremlin spelt it out after talks with us envoys steve witkoff and jared kushner: "a new, long-term architecture of indivisible security and peace. ".

Translated from Kremlin-speak, it means Moscow wants to change the security set-up of Europe in a way that benefits Russia.

What Russia is pushing for is, potentially, the biggest change to European security arrangements since the end of the Cold War.

The Kremlin has put back on the table its controversial proposal from December 2021 â the "draft treaties" with the US and Nato which would not only have put the brakes on the alliance's eastward enlargement by giving Moscow cast-iron guarantees that, for instance, Ukraine and Georgia would never be allowed to join, but also rolled back Nato military infrastructure from countries of central and eastern Europe which became Nato members following the dissolution of the Soviet Union.

Diungkapkan bahwa western leaders dismissed such demands as an unacceptable russian ultimatum. Two months later Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Diungkapkan bahwa the "draft treaties" were put away. Now they are out of the geopolitical filing cabinet, and being quoted again by the Kremlin.

What is more, Yuri Ushakov, Putin's foreign policy aide, has suggested that Moscow is about to "add certain new considerations" to its list of demands in light of Western efforts "to inflict a strategic defeat on Russia".

That does not mean, of course, that Western governments will accept them.

But the fact that the question of European security is featuring now in discussions on Ukraine is viewed here as a victory for Moscow.

"In December 2021 Russia actively proposed that Nato rethink the security system in Europe," wrote newspaper Komsomolskaya Pravda earlier this week.

Diungkapkan bahwa "having secured one victory by forcing the west to think about security, our diplomats need a second by making the west heed russia's concerns about nato enlargement. ".

The EU's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, has called Russia's demands for a new European security architecture a "trap" designed to "shift attention away from a ceasefire".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "the sequencing of ukraine-russia talks is important," kallas wrote on social media. Only then can there be discussions on Europe's wider security architecture. "The priority should be securing a ceasefire, followed by a peace agreement. ".

Europe's problem is that, right now, it is not at the table.

Diungkapkan bahwa moscow has had no desire to give it a chair. It has slammed European leaders for their military support for Kyiv and tough stance on Russia.

This week's peace talks in Abu Dhabi involved Ukraine, Russia and the US.

After his discussions in Moscow, Witkoff indicated that Putin had agreed to the idea of European representatives joining the next round of Ukraine peace talks.

But on Friday the Kremlin indicated a final decision on European participation had not been taken.

"Once we understand their true intentions and their readiness to facilitate the peace process, then it will be possible to take a decision about dialogue on Ukraine in a wider format," said Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov.

Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks.

Europe's security 'fundamentally reshaped' by war in Ukraine.

Inside devastated front-line city that Russia wants Ukraine to give up.

At the talks with Witkoff and Kushner he was sounding uncompromising and confident.

Berdasarkan laporan, the americans are knocking at his door and seeking a deal and the europeans are contemplating contacts with him. Last month the leaders of Norway and Finland reached out and called him.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, and next week in shenzhen, china, on the sidelines of the asia-pacific economic co-operation summit, putin may have a separate meeting with donald trump and xi jinping. Russian media are already comparing them to the "Big Three" - Stalin, Roosevelt and Churchill - who met in 1945 to reorganise post-World War Two Europe.

And yet, after nearly five years of war, Russia has suffered huge losses on the battlefield.

The Russian economy is under increasing pressure.

Ukrainian drone strikes continue to target Russian oil refineries, sparking fears of new fuel shortages.

But, so far, none of this has convinced the Kremlin leader to end the fighting.

#442. Eisenkot accuses Netanyahu of ‘racist’ campaign against Israel’s Arab minority

📅 13 Nov 2026

Eisenkot accuses Netanyahu of ‘racist’ campaign against Israel’s Arab minority

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/13/eisenkot-accuses-netanyahu-of-racist-campaign-against-israels-arab-minority

Statement is rare instance of a prominent Jewish political leader taking a strong stand in defence of Arab Israelis.

Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot accused caretaker premier Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday of fuelling a “racist” campaign against the country’s Arab minority, after he sought to delegitimise the community’s lawmakers by linking them to Hamas.

Eisenkot’s statement was a rare instance of a prominent Jewish political leader taking a strong stand in defence of Arab Israelis, who make up more than 20% of the population.

Two Arab-majority parties, Ra’am and the Joint List, secured a combined 19 seats in last month’s election, winning nearly a sixth of the 120-seat parliament and potentially emerging as kingmakers in efforts by Eisenkot to form a government.

“Arab citizens of Israel are an integral part of the Israeli story,” Eisenkot wrote on X on Friday.

“They have been subjected to a racist and aggressive campaign of delegitimisation, fuelled by the outgoing prime minister and those around him for political purposes,” he added.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the attempt to marginalise them and vilify them collectively is a profound violation of the principles of civic responsibility. ”.

Netanyahu and his allies have repeatedly criticised leaders of Arab parties for refusing to describe Hamas as a “terror group” after its unprecedented 7 October 2023 attack on Israel.

All leaders of Arab parties have condemned the attack, in which Arab Israelis – descendants of Palestinians who remained in what became Israel in 1948 – were also among those killed.

Netanyahu has also repeatedly alleged electoral fraud by Arab-majority parties, but electoral authorities have rejected the claims.

In a speech, Netanyahu lamented that the two Arab lists refused to recognise Israel as a Jewish state, although Ra’am’s leader, Mansour Abbas, has done so in the past.

He further claimed that they sought to establish either an “Islamic state” or a “nationalist Palestinian state”.

During the same ceremony, the national security minister, Itamar Ben Gvir, heckled Joint List’s leader, Yousef Jabareen, during his oath of allegiance, accusing him of having “pledged allegiance to Hamas”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “it is entirely legitimate to disagree with representatives of the arab parties, even to strongly disapprove of some of them. But it is neither legitimate nor acceptable to malign an entire community, and I will not allow it,” Eisenkot said.

President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with forming a new government on Sunday after consultations in which a majority of political parties, including the two Arab lists, recommended him for the role.

But one of Eisenkot’s rightwing allies, Avigdor Lieberman, has said he will back out of the coalition if Arab Israelis are part of it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if eisenkot fails to form a government within 28 days, he may request a 14-day extension. Should he still fall short, the mandate would pass to another lawmaker, most likely Netanyahu.

#444. Nvidia scandal fallout widens as Trump's treasury secretary blames cabinet colleague

📅 13 Nov 2026

Nvidia scandal fallout widens as Trump's treasury secretary blames cabinet colleague

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqvg2d1eg7zro?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

How could the Nvidia CEOâs affair threaten US national security?.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has blamed Howard Lutnick's Commerce Department for failing to properly oversee the export of high-spec AI chips, as the fallout from the Nvidia scandal widens to President Donald Trump's cabinet.

Pressure is building on Lutnick from across the political spectrum to explain his department's actions.

Jensen Huang was ousted as Nvidia CEO after revelations he had an affair with a businesswoman who was also allegedly a Chinese spy.

Megaspeed, the firm she worked for, had been probed by US government agencies over suspicions it was smuggling Nvidia chips into China, reports said, but it is not on a list of firms US companies are prevented from working with.

Bessent told CNBC several agencies "were in favour of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "but commerce has the pen. and you will have to ask them about their internal process," he added.

Bessent's comments come after Lutnick was called to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next month over the Commerce Department's role in allowing Nvidia to export its advanced chips.

Other congressional committees have asked both Lutnick and his department to retain all records relating to Nvidia and Huang.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said some parts of the administration wanted more controls on trade with Megaspeed.

Bessent said he was "frustrated" by delays in putting the company on the export control list and reports of leakage of AI chips into China.

"President Trump made it very clear that China should not receive any Nvidia chips above H100s, so any leakage is very frustrating because it hurts our great companies in the AI race, because it gives the Chinese an advantage," he said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, last year, the commerce department had been investigating megaspeed over suspicions it had been smuggling some of nvidia's advanced ai chips into china, according to the new york times. Megaspeed has been contacted for comment.

There was also pressure on the Commerce Department to add it to the list, but separate reporting in the Financial Times said the department was delaying efforts to have the cloud computing firm included.

However, Bessent also pointed the finger at Nvidia.

"The story has been thus far of Jensen Huang's personal foibles," he told CNBC's Squawk Box programme, external.

"The real story here should be: Did Nvidia know their client, and was there a robust effort at Nvidia to make sure that there was no leakage and that they were selling to what were obviously pass-through shell companies?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "it's important that anyone at the company there be held accountable for that. ".

Bessent's pointed comments are a rare instance of internal debate within the Trump administration spilling out into the public view, although tensions have reportedly simmered between Bessent and Lutnick in the past.

In 2024, the two reportedly jostled for the role of treasury secretary ahead of Trump's return to the White House, and last year the pair butted heads over the administration's tariff policy, accoprding to US media.

How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House.

How AI visionary Jensen Huang was undone by his own bad decisions.

Huang has been summoned to testify before the Senate Banking Committee about his alleged affair with the former Megaspeed executive, who is suspected of being a Chinese spy.

The commerce secretary has also been summoned to appear before the committee in December.

"Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology," committee chairman, Republican Senator Tim Scott posted on X.

Democrats on key congressional committees have asked the Commerce Department and Lutnick to keep all records relating to decisions to allow Nvidia to sell its advanced AI chips to Chinese companies, including all their communications with or about Nvidia and Jensen Huang.

Ways and Means Committee Ranking Member Richard E Neal and Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden are starting investigations into the way Nvidia was allowed to sell these chips.

According to Neal and Wyden, Nvidia's advanced H200 chips could be sold to Chinese firms if they were first imported from their manufacturing facility in Taiwan into America for inspection.

A 25% tariff - a levy that is paid to the federal government - was imposed on those chips, under a section of the Trade Act that Neal and Wyden say is meant to allow the US president to take action against imports that risk national security.

"Trump's use of the statute appears to have done the opposite, undermining US national security and putting Americans at risk," they said.

Who is Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress - and who could take over permanently?.

No personnel, aircraft or infrastructure at Suffolk site affected, says US military.

The US Air Force has said it responded to “suspected unauthorised drone activity” on Friday night at an RAF airbase in the east of England.

No personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected, the air force said.

Sirens were heard at RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk, one of several airbases in the UK used by the US military.

The USAF added: “We continue to work closely with our host nation counterparts to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, US and host nation civilians, contractors and all of our families.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “protecting our shared community is a joint responsibility, and we encourage everyone to support this effort by reporting any unusual or suspicious activity to local authorities. ”.

A UK Ministry of Defence spokesperson said: “We are coordinating with all relevant parties regarding reports of unauthorised drone activity at RAF Lakenheath this evening.

Diungkapkan bahwa “usaf security forces personnel responded to the reports and the situation is now resolved. We will provide updates in due course. We are working closely with them to establish the facts. ”.

The MP for West Suffolk, Nick Timothy, said the authorities at the base had told him “there is no threat to the public, and the incident is now resolved”.

Berdasarkan laporan, he added: “given the raised threat level, i continue to encourage everyone to report anything suspicious or out of the ordinary to the authorities. ”.

RAF Lakenheath said in September it was on “Charlie alert”, the second-highest threat level that can be issued by the US department of defense.

It is home to the 48th fighter wing, also known as the Liberty wing, with almost 7,000 active-duty personnel making it the largest US fighter operation in Europe, according to the official base website.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, earlier this year, police investigated an alleged terror plot at raf fairford in gloucestershire and a trespass incident at raf molesworth in cambridgeshire. Both bases are used by the US Air Force.

In the past two months the US has evacuated planes from RAF Mildenhall in Suffolk and RAF Fairford in response to suspected attacks on the bases allegedly linked to Iran.

Donald Trump said in October that “some threats” led the US to pull its bombers from Fairford.

Police said petrol but no explosives were found during searches of vans near the base in Gloucestershire.

Two men were charged by the Crown Prosecution Service over their alleged involvement in the incident.

This week, at least 12 USAF aircraft departed the nearby RAF Mildenhall base including two Boeing Stratotanker KC-135 refuelling aircraft, with one headed towards Germany and another seen landing at Prestwick airport near Glasgow.

Downing Street insisted earlier this week that British airbases are safe and their security is a “top priority”.

#449. The Peruvian city that has embraced Pope Leo as one of its own

📅 13 Nov 2026

The Peruvian city that has embraced Pope Leo as one of its own

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cwg7l8n7dx5mo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

The Pope, who has Peruvian citizenship, lived in Chiclayo for several years.

Pope Leo XIV has celebrated Mass near the Peruvian city where he made his name as a compassionate bishop who worked closely with poor and migrant communities.

The ceremony was held on Friday at a park in Pimentel, about 10km (six miles) from Chiclayo in northern Peru as part of his tour of Latin America.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the vatican estimates more than 1. 5 million people gathered to welcome the pontiff.

"Thank you for your affection, support and prayers," the Pope told followers.

"Especially for my health during this time of trial which, with God's help, I am overcoming," he added, referencing the surgery he had for lung cancer which took place just weeks ago.

Some of the crowd arrived 12 hours in advance to wait in vigil before the Mass began.

"We spent the night praying, alongside family, excited to welcome the Pope from Chiclayo," said Isa Orderique.

Pope Leo celebrated Mass in front of a jubilant crowd.

Many came from across Peru and even neighbouring countries to attend.

Diungkapkan bahwa merli cruz guerrero, from an area near the ecuadorean border, travelled several hours by bus to attend. She also spent the entire night waiting.

Of all the events the Pope has attended so far during his visit to Peru, this felt particularly emotional.

The crowd fell into a hushed silence as the pontiff's motorcade approached.

They waited eagerly for his arrival despite spending long hours out in the open with the temperature pushing past 30C.

For many living here, the fact that the Pope worked extensively in this region before becoming the head of the Catholic Church has put them in the spotlight.

"The Pope has come home and Chiclayo is celebrating," said Lisbeth DÃ­az, a teacher who worked with Pope Leo when he served as the city's bishop between 2015 and 2023.

Lisbeth DÃ­az says Chiclayo is celebrating the Pope's return.

Peru is the longest stop on the first tour of Latin America by the pontiff, who was elected in May 2025.

The trip has also taken in Argentina and Uruguay, but his time in this country carries particular significance.

The Pope not only lived in Peru for long periods between 1985 and 2023 but also became a citizen of the country in 2015, forging close ties with local communities.

Around Chiclayo, it is hard to meet anyone who doesn't claim to be a friend of the Pope or have a special anecdote about him.

Sebagaimana diketahui, some recall how he would enjoy sampling peruvian delicacies at el trã©bol, a restaurant next to the city's cathedral. Others remember his love of tennis.

But for many it's the more serious moments of his time here, such as helping launch soup kitchens during the Covid-19 pandemic, or wading through deep waters on horseback when floods hit the area.

Several of these images are on display in a small museum dedicated to him at the entrance to the bishop's residence.

Commemorative pictures of the Pope are sold in the main of square of Chiclayo, including a famous image of him visiting a remote village on horseback.

But for the city, and for a country that calls him the "Peruvian Pope", his return home means much more than a collection of photographs and anecdotes.

"It is the return of the man who brought Peruvians closer to the Church," said Samuel David Miranda Atoche, a local parish priest from Chiclayo who was ordained by the Pope back when he was still the bishop and known under his birth name of Robert Prevost.

And it is not just local people he connected with, according to DÃ­az, who came to Chiclayo from Venezuela.

"It was difficult for him to see so many migrants living on the streets," she added, recalling the time when large numbers of Venezuelans came through Chiclayo escaping the political and economic crisis in their home country.

#451. Rip out ugly clutter to help revive UK high streets, says thinktank

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/nov/13/rip-out-clutter-to-retail-revive-high-streets-thinktank

Exclusive: Report says restricting cars and freeing up pavement space could be a cheap way to bring shoppers back.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the long decline of the high street is a problem that has gripped british governments for years. But what if there was a solution no one had considered before – doing it all on the cheap?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, spending less money is, admittedly, just one element of a report led by the urban thinktank create streets. But it does argue that rather than multimillion-pound revamps, a better answer could be smaller changes aimed at making town and city centres more appealing.

Central to this, the study says, is trying to banish, or at least tame, motor traffic, because too often urban centres are places “designed to be driven through, not for time to be spent in”.

As well as citing a lack of imagination, the report, which is co-produced by bike storage company Cyclehoop, blames planning regulations that favour conformity and clutter and too often treat speeding cars as a given, to which everything else must adjust.

“The default high street is engineered for traffic and furnished from a catalogue: a tarmac pavement, guardrails penning people at the kerb, litter bins ordered from a procurement catalogue, a row of plastic planters – public investment that is joyless,” it says.

While planners have traditionally focused on car access as a metric for thriving town centres, calculations for the Create Streets report suggest that replacing parking with other kerbside infrastructure, including bike spaces or outside drinking and dining areas, creates more economic value.

Berdasarkan laporan, it found that one parking space in the high street of a market town is typically used by about 3. 5 vehicles a day, bringing in just over £73,000 a year in spending to nearby shops.

But the same 12 square metres, if used to hold nine share e-bikes, generates an average of 13 trips a day, with over £146,000 a year in spending, even taking into account the lower average spend per person.

In a busier city, where share bikes would be used more frequently, the estimated total annual spend rises to more than £300,000.

Repurposing the space for outside dining brings less dramatic gains, but in a city centre it can still amount to about £120,000 in extra annual spending.

The report calls for a cultural rethink involving low-cost tweaks that rip away ugly and unnecessary street furniture and make better use of kerbsides.

Calling use by families “the indicator species of a healthy high street”, the report cites what is known as “the wrist test” – whether it feels safe to let go of a young child’s wrist so they can roam with some freedom.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this is best done, it argues, by removing the threat of speeding motor vehicles and not by trying to mitigate their impact. It calls the removal of pedestrian guardrails next to roads “the most cost-effective upgrade for the majority of high streets”, saying they are an eyesore with minimal safety benefits.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the report says “the absurdity of modern public realm management” is exemplified by secured by design, policy guidelines on cutting neighbourhood crime. These can, critics point out, mean benches and plants are removed on the advice of police, supposedly to discourage antisocial behaviour.

Andy Burnham, the prime minister, has pledged to try to reverse the decline of high streets, announcing in September a £210m regeneration fund.

Sign up for the Breaking News UK email to get newsletter alerts direct to your inbox.

However, the bulk of the money will go into buildings: turning old shops into shared workspaces or community cafes, or keeping pubs and clubs in business.

Berdasarkan laporan, the report argues that renovating buildings is pointless if the street outside is unappealing. To reduce clutter, it says, there should be “a presumption of removal where an item cannot be justified”.

The effects can be dramatic, the report says, pointing to examples including Altrincham in Cheshire, where the creation of a walkable, car-free urban area helped see retail vacancies fall from over 30% to 7% in less than a decade.

Such initiatives do not have to be expensive, it claims, noting the example of an unused patch of land next to a church in Grimsby which was turned into a park for less than £20,000.

“Streets that are ugly are not so because councils lack the desire to change them, but because the system is counting the maintenance liabilities, not the benefits,” said David Milner of Create Streets.

“What works is cheap: trees in the ground, benches people want to sit on, clutter taken away.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “so much of what is built now seems to be temporary, looking more like road works than public realm improvements, so we encourage the concept of permanence; more trees in the ground, not in giant plant pots, for example. ”.

A spokesperson for the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government said: “We support local leaders to make decisions on pedestrianisation based on their communities’ needs.

“Our Hope on the High Street strategy will help local people revive town centres by protecting community assets, bringing derelict buildings back into use and tackling the spread of vape and gambling shops.

Diungkapkan bahwa “funding is available for local leaders to spend on their priorities, including pedestrianising and regenerating their high streets if they so wish. ”.

In future, German spies working for the BND foreign intelligence service will be able to conduct covert operations abroad.

Germany's foreign and domestic intelligence services are to be given greater powers to combat espionage, terrorism and sabotage after the country's parliament, the Bundestag, approved a major overhaul of its legislation.

Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt, who championed the bill, has called it a "reform of the century", necessary because of the increasing threats from foreign powers.

But the Left Party's security spokeswoman, Clara BÃ¼nger, said Dobrindt was creating a new German secret police.

The legislation gives numerous new powers to Germany's BND federal intelligence service, and its BfV domestic service, the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution.

In the Bundestag, 309 MPs voted in favour of the new law on intelligence services, while 190 voted against and 71 abstained.

For historical reasons, German intelligence has mainly focused on gathering information rather than acting on it.

In future, German spies working for the BND, which is responsible for foreign intelligence, will be able to conduct covert operations abroad, including sabotage.

This could include paralysing the servers of state-sponsored hacker groups, disrupting disinformation networks, or even disrupting supply chains for weapons.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, agents for the domestic intelligence service, the bfv, will no longer to be limited to gathering information. For the first time they will be able to take protective action against property and IT systems, if specific threats are identified.

That means they will be allowed to dismantle or break explosives or weapons, divert or block data flows during cyber-attacks, delete or falsify data stored for malicious purposes, and plant false information on those involved.

The government says the reform is needed because of an increase in foreign espionage, particularly from Russia, China and Iran.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "we are the target of hybrid threats," said dobrindt. "Germany is a theatre of operations for terrorism, extremism and foreign powers. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, in august, a drone carrying an explosive device was discovered at leipzig airport, close to ukrainian cargo planes. However, it failed to explode as the bomb's detonator was apparently faulty.

German authorities say Russia was behind the attack.

The new law has been bitterly criticised by some opposition politicians, even though Dobrindt has said it is "madness" to think it means that Germany is creating a new secret police.

And Clara BÃ¼nger from the Left Party told public broadcaster ARD that the new law was "a monsterâ¦ summoning ghosts that we will probably never be able to get rid of".

The separation between the police and the secret service, she warned, was "being eroded" - and BÃ¼nger said that had been a lesson learned from the Nazi era.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "this means the secret service is being granted executive powers and will not only be allowed to act pre-emptively, but will also be granted police powers. ".

However, Sonja Eichwede of the centre-left SPD, which is part of Germany's governing coalition, said the reforms would make a significant contribution to ensuring the country's democracy was "robust and resilient".

The government’s plans to release thousands of prisoners early were dealt a blow on Friday after probation officers across England and Wales voted to strike over pay and excessive workloads.

Sebagaimana diketahui, members of the union, napo, backed overtime restrictions and other forms of action short of a strike, which is likely to start on 23 november. Plans are being made for strike action to follow at a later stage.

The union, whose members work across probation offices and in family courts, said it launched its ballot because of an “inadequate” 5% pay offer from ministers and a failure to cut workloads.

Probation officers have come under increasing pressure since the launch of the latest early release scheme in October, which is meant to ease overcrowding in prisons.

They are responsible for monitoring offenders’ behaviour, overseeing their rehabilitation, monitoring their electronic tags and recalling them to prison for any offences or licence breaches, such as entering an exclusion or restriction zone protecting victims.

By the end of the year, about 2,500 offenders, some of whom are sex offenders, domestic abusers and stalkers, will be released under the scheme.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the union had sought a 12% increase. Diungkapkan bahwa “the vote also reflects serious anger at the state of probation workloads, which were already in crisis before the latest version of the prisoner early release scheme. ”.

Napo said probation wages have “stagnated” since 2010, with reception staff on a salary just above the minimum wage – the lowest in the civil service.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on pay, napo members voted by 85% in favour of action short of strike action and 74% in favour of strike action. In a ballot on workloads, the vote was 87% in favour of action short of strike action and 75% in favour of strikes.

The Ministry of Justice is recruiting an additional 1,300 trainee probation officers for the 2026-27 financial year as part of a £700m investment package extending through 2028-29.

Chris Van Hollen (L) says he will challenge Chuck Schumer (R) and that the Democrats need new leadership.

Senator Chuck Schumer is facing a challenge to his position as US Senate majority leader from his fellow Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen, as the party prepares to take control of Congress after sweeping the midterm elections.

Van Hollen, 67, said in a post on X on Thursday that Americans voted for change earlier this month and "to deliver, we need new leadership".

Berdasarkan laporan, schumer, 75, has led democrats in the chamber since 2017, serving as both majority and minority leader. He was first elected to the Senate in 1999.

Following the midterms earlier this month, his position has come under pressure by some left-wing Democrats who see him as too moderate and part of the party establishment.

Responding to the challenge, Schumer, who represents New York, said he welcomed "any discussion about the future of our caucus and the important work ahead".

He added that he was "proud of what we've accomplished together" in the midterms, and he had "the votes to continue as Democratic leader".

The vote on Senate leader will be held behind closed doors in early December and the winner will assume the role on 4 January, when Democrats take control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives after their midterms successes.

The move by Van Hollen, who represents Maryland, marks the most significant step by a high-profile Democrat to challenge the party's existing leadership following last week's midterms victory.

Announcing his plans to run in a post on X, he wrote that Americans had called on the party to "unrig an economy rigged against working people".

Berdasarkan laporan, "we should not be preserving our institutions if they are not delivering for the american people," he said at a summit in colorado hosted by majority democrats. "And we should be making delivering for the American people the single mission of our government, even when that means shaking things up. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa he added: "this country does not belong to the people who can afford to buy influence. And it's time we govern like that. It belongs to all of us. ".

In recent years, Van Hollen has taken positions popular with those on the left of his party.

In 2024, he supported restricting weapons shipments to Israel and criticised the Biden administration over its role in the war in Gaza.

In an interview with MS NOW, Van Hollen - who has served in the Senate for nearly a decade - acknowledged that he was an "underdog" but added that he believed the race was "very much in flux".

Independent Senator Bernie Sanders and Democratic Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed have both publicly come out in support of Van Hollen - while others have also called for new leadership.

In a post on X, Sanders said he believed Van Hollen "will stand up to powerful special interests, take on the billionaire class and fight for working families".

El-Sayed said the challenger would bring "bold leadership" and lead with both "courage and experience".

Others Democrats have publicly backed Schumer.

Senator Jacky Rosen of Nevada said: "He has the experience and the fight to continue leading our diverse caucus at this crucial moment".

Berdasarkan laporan, senator kirsten gillibrand said: "you will see, despite all the grumblings, enormous gratitude for the hard work he has done to get us to this position. ".

#461. Walliams allegations prompt calls for staggered age of consent at 16 and 17

📅 13 Nov 2026

Walliams allegations prompt calls for staggered age of consent at 16 and 17

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/law/2026/nov/13/staggered-age-of-consent-16-17-law

Barrister say law does not adequately recognise power imbalance between young people and much older adults.

Allegations against Russell Brand and, separately, David Walliams, which he denies, have led to calls for greater legal protection for 16- and 17-year-olds from sexual exploitation by older adults.

Berdasarkan laporan, a staggered consent law is one route favoured by campaigners, supported by some labour mps. Claire Waxman, the victims’ commissioner for England and Wales, has called for “serious conversations” on the potential for legislative change.

The barrister Charlotte Proudman, who specialises in law regarding violence against women and girls, said: “Staggered, or graduated, age of consent means that the law takes account of the age difference between sexual partners, rather than treating 16 as the point at which a child can legally consent to sexual activity with someone of any age.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “a sexual relationship between a 16-year-old and an 18-year-old is fundamentally different from one between a 16-year-old girl and a 50-year-old man. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a 16-year-old cannot buy alcohol or cigarettes, but someone decades older can legally have sex with them. “The law does not adequately recognise the significant power imbalance between children and much older adults, particularly where grooming, financial dependence, celebrity status or emotional manipulation are involved,” Proudman said.

A move to staggered consent “would place responsibility on the older adult”, she said, rather than requiring a teenage complainant to demonstrate grooming, coercion or exploitation.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “this is not about denying young people sexual autonomy,” she said. “It is about recognising that consent must be understood in the context of age, maturity, vulnerability and power. ”.

The Close the Consent Gap campaign proposes a staggered age of consent making it a criminal offence for a 16- or 17-year-old to consent to sexual activity with anyone more than three years their senior.

“For example, a consensual relationship between two teenagers close in age would remain lawful, whereas sexual activity between a 16-year-old and a 35-year-old would be prohibited,” said the campaign’s founder, Layla Stone.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “every other framework of the law recognises 16- and 17-year-olds as children. We want the law to recognise children – 16 and 17 years old – as children who need to be protected in all frameworks of the law. ”.

Stone said there could be a “huge power imbalance” between a 16-year-old living at home and a 21-year-old with money and independence.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the law on the issue in the rest of the world is complex and varied. Some countries have extra safeguards built in for 16- and 17-year-olds. Canada, for example, recognises age difference as a factor in determining exploitation for this age group. For 14- and 15-year-olds, Canadian law criminalises any sexual activity if a partner is five or more years older.

Prof Roger Ingham, the director of the Centre for Sexual Health Research at the University of Southampton, said: “My question, as a researcher, is: what is the evidence that it actually works or doesn’t work to protect young people?”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he said there was no strong evidence that different countries with different ages had completely different patterns of sexual behaviour or outcomes. But he said it was a difficult question to answer “because a lot of these cases are simply not reported”.

Ingham said “tinkering with the law” could divert attention from other efforts, including better sex education, and risked young people avoiding seeking contraceptive advice, or other support they needed, if their relationship was deemed illegal.

Dr Sophie King-Hill, an associate professor at the University of Birmingham researching sexual behaviour of children and young people, said people were “looking for fixes, looking for blame, looking for gaps in the law”, but she also questioned where the evidence was that it worked.

“If we’re looking at preventing grooming and preventing young people being exploited, we’ve got to be really careful not to confuse this changing of the law with solving the problem,” she said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “grooming, coercion, manipulation and abuse of power don’t suddenly begin at 16. People feel like they need to do something, and I’m not necessarily opposed to it in its totality, but I think it’s really naive to see it as such a solution to something that’s really complex and complicated within society. I can see where it’s coming from. ”.

King-Hill said it could create a false sense of protection for young people, and it risked children and young people not coming forward “because they’ll be worried they’ve broken the law”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i think from my research perspective and the work that i’ve carried out, you’ve got to do things like this really carefully, because you can inadvertently make things worse or oversimplify a very complex and complicated problem. ”.

Families clear homes of David Walliams books after sexual offence allegations

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/nov/13/families-clear-homes-of-david-walliams-books-after-sexual-offence-allegations

Parents take action while several independent bookshops say they had already stopped stocking his titles.

Diungkapkan bahwa in sarah’s house, david walliams has been a bedtime staple for years. Her children, aged eight, six and four, have dressed up as his characters for World Book Day – they love the over-the-top, unusual names and illustrations.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, now, all the books are going. “I’ll probably take them away and replace them with other authors,” says Sarah, a mother in west London. “Sooner rather than later, so they don’t realise. ” If any of her children ask why, she will tell them “that his choices aren’t great and that I think we should be reading other books”.

Diungkapkan bahwa this week a joint guardian and itv news investigation alleged that the children’s author used his position to pursue young women and girls for sex, including girls as young as 15. Walliams denies the allegations. HarperCollins stopped publishing new Walliams books last December and dropped his entire backlist in September.

For many independent children’s booksellers, the news only confirmed a decision made long ago.

Berdasarkan laporan, helen tamblyn-saville, owner of wonderland bookshop in retford, nottinghamshire, stopped stocking him in 2020. “They didn’t fit the ethos and values of my shop,” she says. Walliams’s books “punched down”, she believes, citing what she sees as “themes of racism, misogyny and classism” in his writings.

In 2021, HarperCollins removed a story about a Chinese boy – Brian Wong, Who Was Never, Ever Wrong – from future editions of The World’s Worst Children after complaints that it relied on harmful racial stereotypes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in 2025, tamblyn-saville turned down an invitation to an event with him. “It feels very much as if the golden goose had to be protected, despite the clear red flags. ”.

Griffin Books in Penarth, south Wales, dropped his books about 18 months ago over “the low quality of the writing and his frequent use of offensive stereotypes”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the chicken and frog bookshop in brentwood, essex, has not stocked him for a decade. Urmi, owner of Pickled Pepper Books in north London, has a blunter opinion: “We heard [rumours] about David Walliams at least five years ago and at that point chose to not stock his books,” she says. She believes that “everyone in the industry knew … so anyone that’s only just taking books off the shelf is only interested in profit”.

Diungkapkan bahwa mainstream stores have moved quickly. The Works, a budget retailer, said it had removed all David Walliams titles from sale and TG Jones confirmed it no longer sold his books in store or online. Waterstones said it was talking to HarperCollins about returning “the small number of copies which remain in stock in a few of our shops”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, families are clearing their shelves too. One parent walked past a neighbourhood book-swap box this week and found it stuffed full of Walliams titles. Another mother joked that she would be burning hers, saying Walliams was “a knock-off Roald Dahl anyway”. Sarah hasn’t decided what to do with hers: giving them to a charity shop just puts them “back into the system”.

Diungkapkan bahwa walliams’ sales have been falling sharply – but they have not disappeared. Retailers sold 7,497 Walliams books over the past four weeks, worth £48,400, according to NielsenIQ BookData figures reported by The Bookseller.

Berdasarkan laporan, in the same period last year, when he had a new book out, walliams sold 102,000. Even so, almost 108,000 copies of his books have been sold so far this year, worth more than £702,000, and his titles have made more than £153m since 2008.

Sign up for the Breaking News UK email to get newsletter alerts direct to your inbox.

Sebagaimana diketahui, public libraries are also facing a difficult decision. “This is a very sensitive issue involving deeply disturbing allegations, and some people may find the continued presence of these books upsetting,” said Isobel Hunter, CEO of the charity Libraries Connected.

“But we also have a long-established legal principle within the sector that all books should be available to the public unless the content itself is unlawful.

Berdasarkan laporan, “so most library services have said that the books will remain in their collections until they are naturally weeded out and withdrawn under existing stock policy. That doesn’t mean, of course, that libraries are obliged to promote them or have them on display. ”.

Anecdotally, she said, demand had “dropped significantly in recent years”.

Some schools appear to be taking a harder line – several teachers told the Guardian they were removing Walliams books from their classroom shelves.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for sarah, the principle is simple: “kids need to understand that actions have consequences. If something’s not right, then we need to act upon it. ”.

The site of a car explosion that wounded Sergei Zavorotny in Moscow.

A car bomb attack in Moscow has wounded a former adviser to Ukrainian ex-prime minister Mykola Azarov, Russia's Investigative Committee says.

Sergei Zavorotny, now a journalist and commentator, was behind the wheel of his black Toyota when the explosion happened and Azarov told Russian TV his condition in hospital was "rather critical".

The car bomb went off a day after a Russian colonel was killed in another explosion in St Petersburg, and both blasts are seen as part of a series of attacks on military and prominent figures linked to Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Zavorotny, 72, worked as a press aide to Mykola Azarov in Kyiv until 2014.

But when pro-Kremlin Ukrainian president Viktor Yanukovych was toppled from power, Azarov fled Kyiv for Russia and tried unsuccessfully to set up a government in exile.

In a 2020 US Senate report on interference in the 2016 American presidential election, Zavorotny is described at the time as an SVR [Russian foreign intelligence] officer involved in influence operations.

Diungkapkan bahwa russia's investigative committee said on telegram on friday: "serhiy zavorotny, a former adviser to the former ukrainian prime minister mykola azarov, was injured while driving a car. He was taken to one of the city hospitals, where he is receiving medical care. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, it added: "a set of necessary investigative actions is being carried out. A number of examinations will be appointed, including medical and explosives. ".

According to several unconfirmed reports, Zavorotny suffered a number of serious injuries after an explosive device was detonated remotely.

Russia said the car bombs are the latest in a series of attacks targeting pro-Kremlin figures.

On Thursday a car bomb in the Pushkinsky District of St Petersburg killed a member of the Russian military, again after it was attached to the base of the car and detonated remotely.

The man targeted in the attack is yet to be named officially, but reputable sources suggest he was a high-ranking figure in the 6th Guards Air and Air Defence Forces Army.

Overnight into Friday, Ukraine and Russia exchanged attacks on each other's territories.

Ukrainian authorities said a hospital had been targeted by Russian bombardment.

They added that three people, including a 17-year-old boy, were also killed in attacks across southern Odesa and Zaporizhzhia.

Russia said a Ukrainian strike on an industrial facility in the central Samara region killed four people.

Berdasarkan laporan, and in the southern volgograd region another four died after an industrial zone was hit by drones. A further person died in the Bryansk border region, an area that is often fired upon.

Ukraine said these were retaliatory attacks in response to Russia's persistent targeting of its cities.

The crash took place on a highway bordering Kaziranga National Park in the Golaghat district of Assam.

At least 24 people have died and 11 others injured after a bus collided with a truck in Assam, north-east India.

The accident happened near Kaziranga National Park, a Unesco World Heritage site, and the injured have been admitted to Jorhat Medical College and Hospital.

Several of the deceased are college students, according to Assam's rural development minister Atul Bora, but they have not yet been publicly identified.

Bora added that witnesses reported one of the vehicles may have been speeding when the crash took place, but "the exact reason will be known after [an investigation]".

Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma wrote in a post on X that "the scale of this loss has shaken all of us".

Sebagaimana diketahui, he adds: "our foremost priority now is to make sure the injured receive the best possible medical care without delay. ".

Family members of one of the victims pictured at the accident site.

The bus was carrying passengers from Bokakhat and was headed towards Nagaon.

Bokakhat is best known as the gateway to Kaziranga National Park, famous for its one-horned rhinoceroses.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, nagaon is an important agricultural and commercial centre in central assam, about 120km (74. 5 miles) west of Bokakhat by road.

Lurinjyoti Gogoi, chief of a regional opposition party, said road safety has long been a major concern in the state.

"The government must take it up seriously," he said.

Road accidents are responsible for thousands of deaths in India every year.

In 2023, 172,000 people lost their lives on Indian roads, or 474 a day â roughly one every three minutes.

The count increased to 183,382 deaths in 2025.

Experts say the crisis is rooted not just in infrastructure but in human behaviour, enforcement gaps and systemic neglect.

#478. Nationwide FAA ground stop: nearly 11,000 flights delayed or canceled at airports across the US

📅 13 Nov 2026

Nationwide FAA ground stop: nearly 11,000 flights delayed or canceled at airports across the US

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/13/faa-nationwide-ground-stop-flights

Transportation secretary said stoppage is due to ‘communication issue’ and homeland security says there’s no indication of ‘nefarious attack’.

Flights grounded at all US airports due to communications outage – live.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has issued a nationwide ground stop for all flights that are due to take off in the US on Friday, delaying or canceling more than 11,000 US flights, according to aviation tracker FlightAware.

In a post on X, Sean Duffy, the US transportation secretary, said the stoppage is due to “a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers” and that the FAA’s technicians are looking into the matter.

A notice from the FAA said the ground stop was being imposed “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety”.

Markwayne Mullin, the Department of Homeland security director, said in a news conference that preliminary investigations into the stoppage do not indicate that it was tied to a “nefarious attack”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “there’s no indication as of yet that this was a nefarious attack against it. It’s just a telecommunications outage as of right now,” he told reporters.

After restoring communications so all airborne flights can land, Mullin said, “we’re going to continue to work to find out what the root of the cause is”.

“We’re not ruling out anything at this point,” Mullin added.

Mullin said the immediate priority was ensuring that planes still in the air would be landing safely, but that there was no clear information on how long the stoppage might last.

Berdasarkan laporan, in a statement, the los angeles mayor, karen bass, said that she was aware of the stoppage and getting updates on it. Los Angeles is home to LAX, the fifth-busiest airport in the US, according to the bureau of transportation statistics.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i am in close contact with leadership at los angeles world airports (lawa) to receive real-time updates and assess impacts. We will continue to monitor this evolving situation and work closely with federal and state partners. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, at ronald reagan washington national airport, gate agents, along with most travelers in the terminal, refreshed their phones looking for updates, and attempted to change their flights. Nearly every seat was filled, with some people sitting on the floor and using their luggage as makeshift desks for their laptops.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a ground-stop order by the faa requires that aircraft remain on the ground and bars them from taking off. Planes already in the air are usually allowed to remain in the air. This is the third time all departing flights have been grounded in the US. The first time was on 11 September 2001; the other was in January 2023, when the FAA paused all ⁠domestic departures for less than two hours after a pilot notification system malfunctioned.

The FAA has more than 14,000 air traffic controllers who handle the more than 44,000 flights that take off from airports across the US each day, according to FAA data.

Last week, the FAA announced that the first digital air traffic control towers in the US are officially operational in Alaska and Florida, as part of its ongoing modernization project that is meant to reduce flight delays and improve the flow of air traffic.

Sebagaimana diketahui, last year, ​congress ​approved $12. 5bn to fix ​the FAA’s ageing communications system, and ​on Friday ‌the FAA ​and ​White House asked Congress for another $30. 1bn to address other issues.

#480. How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore

📅 13 Nov 2026

How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ck1exevgql4qo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Singapore has painstakingly cultivated a reputation as an open, business-friendly economy.

A major scandal involving Nvidia founder Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy based in Singapore has cast a spotlight on the city-state's success as a global chip hub - and a location for alleged illicit trade.

Sebagaimana diketahui, on thursday, huang stepped down from the us chip giant after admitting he had an affair. He was reportedly involved with a woman named Alice Huang, who ran Singaporean data centre company Megaspeed, a major buyer of Nvidia's chips.

For decades, Singapore has painstakingly cultivated a reputation as an open, business-friendly economy offering easy access to both the US and Chinese markets.

With the AI boom, it has become a major hub for the trade of high-end semiconductor chips in recent years.

Singapore was the second-largest billing centre globally last year for Nvidia, accounting for nearly a fifth of what the US chip giant earns.

But notably, less than 1% of its earnings were for chips that actually entered Singapore, as the island acts as a hub for many Asian companies to place orders and send them elsewhere.

Since 2022, when the US restricted advanced American semiconductors from being exported to China or acquired by Chinese companies, US officials have been concerned that other countries such as Singapore could be used by Chinese companies to gain access to the chips.

It became the biggest buyer of Nvidia's chips in South East Asia and is suspected of giving backdoor access to these chips to Chinese companies via its data centres in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.

While Singapore does not prohibit the transfer of advanced AI chips to companies abroad, such moves can breach US export controls.

Singapore has said that while it does not enforce "unilateral export controls imposed by other countries" it expects all companies in its jurisdiction to respect such regulations.

The city-state has had some success in policing this.

It has charged four companies and five individuals - including Chinese nationals - for various offences including fraud, following US concerns that Chinese AI company DeepSeek had been buying Nvidia chips from third parties in Singapore, among other places.

They also tried to probe Megaspeed, but were faced with a number of difficulties.

In a statement released on Thursday, the government said that since February 2025, they had been looking into whether Megaspeed and other firms had made false declarations about data servers which were purchased and exported through Singapore.

The companies stated the equipment would end up in neighbouring Malaysia, but Singapore authorities suspect the equipment's final destinations were elsewhere.

Singapore said it sought assistance from US authorities several times to get more information from one of the investigated companies - Supermicro, a US-based company which the BBC understands was supplying computer servers to Megaspeed.

Berdasarkan laporan, but "despite these repeated requests, singapore has to date received limited information or assistance", it said in its statement. The BBC has sought comment from the US State Department.

Singapore authorities said they had also investigated Alice Huang - not for espionage, but for any possible role in Megaspeed's suspected fraud.

In the end, they found "insufficient evidence" of crime and let her leave Singapore in February this year, after holding her passport for several months.

Since launching their probe nearly two years ago, Singapore has yet to bring any charges against Megaspeed or any of the companies and individuals linked to the case.

Singapore and US investigations into Megaspeed are still ongoing.

In 2024, US officials had paid a visit to a Malaysian data centre owned by Megaspeed and saw Nvidia technology still in their boxes, raising concerns that Megaspeed was shipping high-end chips out elsewhere, according to a report by the New York Times.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, last year, megaspeed appeared to have imported 50,000 more chips than nvidia could account for, according to a bloomberg report. Nvidia later adjusted its own figures after visiting more warehouses.

Megaspeed has maintained it has always acted lawfully and that previous inspections by authorities found no evidence of illegal activity.

On Thursday, the company said it "welcomes appropriate government scrutiny" and that it is "committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government".

China has also long refuted accusations that its companies and institutions are illegally obtaining high-end US chips.

Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia on Thursday following a board meeting.

How Megaspeed and Alice Huang came to Singapore highlights other vulnerabilities stemming from the city-state's openness.

Diungkapkan bahwa in recent years, the city-state has become a prime destination for chinese companies, with tech firms such as tiktok and manus making it their global headquarters. Besides Singapore's ease of doing business, it has a population that is mostly ethnically Chinese and largely views China positively.

For a Chinese firm, Singapore offers a base near the mainland and a "neutral address" that global customers and investors accept, said Winston Ma, adjunct professor at New York University's School of Law.

But critics say this has given rise to "Singapore-washing", where Chinese companies use the city-state's clean image to obscure their origins, reduce suspicions and even cover up dubious activities.

Washington-based security analysis group C4ADS told the BBC they had assessed Alice Huang's setup of Megaspeed to be such a case.

BBC checks of corporate records in China, Hong Kong and Singapore found that in 2019, Huang sold a gaming company and its subsidiaries to Chinese gaming firm 7Road.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in march 2023, a 7road subsidiary in singapore named huang as its executive director. The next day it changed its name - to Megaspeed.

Huang was in charge for eight months before she transferred the company to a Singaporean man.

During this period, Megaspeed went through "a critical period of corporate restructuring and regional expansion", and her corporate relationships raised questions about whether "Megaspeed's Singaporean identity is genuine or effectively Chinese-controlled", according to C4ADS.

Even after she transferred Megaspeed, C4ADS assessed that she was still "practically in control" of the company, based on her links to Megaspeed via another company as well as LinkedIn posts where she continued to identify herself as Megaspeed's "chairwoman" at conferences.

Megaspeed has not answered BBC queries regarding the company's and Alice Huang's links to China and the Chinese government.

Alice Huang, seen here in Taipei with Jensen Huang last year, ran Megaspeed for several months in 2023.

All this reinforces the dilemma faced by Singapore.

"For the longest time, Singapore has managed to enjoy the best of both worlds with excellent relations with US and China," Nanyang Technological University politics and international studies lecturer Dylan Loh said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, singapore has long positioned itself as a neutral party between the two superpowers. Its prime minister Lawrence Wong has insisted that his country is neither pro-China nor pro-America, but "pro-Singapore".

But Loh says this balancing act "has now fast become very difficult to manage and sometimes quite fraught too" with the US-China dispute over chips.

With the Megaspeed case, the tightrope Singapore has walked is set to get even narrower, according to analysts.

Beijing may ask why Singapore is investigating issues pertaining to US restrictions and whether they are siding with the US' interests, says Chong Ja Ian, a Singaporean political scientist and non-resident scholar with Carnegie China.

Washington, in turn, might read Singapore's latest statement as "pushing blame" on the US, which could lead to backlash from the White House, he said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "singapore has made a policy position not to take sides. But by not choosing a side, they run the risk of being seen as complicit" in either side's agenda, he said.

But Benjamin Ho, an assistant professor and China expert at Singapore's S Rajaratnam School of International Studies, noted that this was "not the first or last time Singapore will be caught between the US and China".

Diungkapkan bahwa "this is the price that an open economy has to grapple with - you get caught in the middle when things turn sour. ".

Additional reporting by Jack Lau of the BBC's Global China Unit.

#482. Tanker collides with cruise ship on Mississippi River in New Orleans

📅 13 Nov 2026

Tanker collides with cruise ship on Mississippi River in New Orleans

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/13/mississippi-river-crash-new-orleans

Large emergency response under way to rescue people from the water, with overnight cruise ship on its side.

New Orleans river collision – latest updates.

A tanker collided with a river cruise ship docked on the Mississippi River in New Orleans on Friday afternoon, prompting an emergency effort to rescue people from the water, according to officials.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the atlantic asphalt tanker collided with american cruise lines’ american heritage at about 12. 30pm, said Kimberly Curth, the Port of New Orleans press secretary, in a statement.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the american heritage had about 129 passengers – in addition to crew members – onboard when it was hit, according to curth. About two hours before that, the American Heritage had docked at the port to begin passenger disembarkation, Curth said.

A statement from the office of the New Orleans mayor, Helena Moreno, on Friday afternoon said that “multiple individuals have been rescued”.

An emergency response source said that there were efforts under way – including by New Orleans firefighters – to rescue multiple people from the water.

“Public safety agencies are coordinating response efforts, with the immediate priority being the safety and rescue of those involved,” the statement from Moreno’s office said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, officials did not immediately provide details about the circumstances of the crash. The emergency response source said it was possible the tanker had lost power before striking the American Heritage, but that had not been confirmed.

Diungkapkan bahwa the website marinetraffic. com showed the Atlantic Asphalt’s path was uneventful as it went around the Mississippi River bend near New Orleans’ Algiers Point neighborhood. It had just made it past the Crescent City Connection bridge linking New Orleans’ central business district and the Algiers section when it began drifting to its starboard – or right – side.

Diungkapkan bahwa video showed it hit the side of the american heritage, which slowly rolled toward where it was struck. One witness, Jamie Holford, told local NBC News affiliate WDSU that it took 15 minutes “from impact to where it rolled over”.

“Surreal – that’s what that was,” Holford said.

Maritime law expert Martin J Davies of New Orleans’ Tulane University told local Fox affiliate WVUE that the Atlantic Asphalt was lucky to have not hit the Crescent City Connection, which is estimated to carry about 160,000 cars daily.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “this is obviously a really bad, incident,” davies said. “But it could also have struck the bridge, which it didn’t. ”.

A video from WDSU showed crew members of a tugboat working to pull people in lifejackets or holding on to flotation rings out of the river.

Berdasarkan laporan, video from wvue showed the american heritage slowly rolling on to its side with the atlantic asphalt nearby. One image on social media showed people climbing on the side of the cruise boat – specifically, on stateroom balconies – after it was struck, with chairs and tables strewn about.

People who had gotten off the American Heritage after it was struck were being brought inside the New Orleans port’s administration building.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the operator of new orleans’ university medical center, lcmc, reported on friday that there were 24 patients admitted to the hospital from the crash. The local Acadian Ambulance service took eight people from there to the hospital to be treated for injuries, the details of which were not immediately available, agency spokesperson Caitlin Russo said.

Rescue-related activity on the river had significantly scaled back later on Friday afternoon in the hours after the crash.

Beside New Orleans firefighters and port and city police, the US Coast Guard and local emergency medical services personnel were at the scene conducting rescue and response operations, Curth’s statement said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a statement from the us coast guard said the river “is closed to all vessel traffic between mile markers 93 and 96”, encompassing the area where friday’s crash occurred. That is so to assist responders as they “assess the situation and conduct response operations”, the statement said.

Berdasarkan laporan, a statement from american cruise lines on friday said “guests and crew were evacuated” from the american heritage but did not provide numbers. “We are deeply concerned for everyone involved,” the cruise operator’s statement added.

Berdasarkan laporan, the american heritage, a 300ft paddle-wheel ship, was built in 2015 and previously sailed as the queen of the mississippi. It has more than 80 staterooms and operates cruises on the Mississippi River, including ones which depart from New Orleans.

Diungkapkan bahwa the atlantic asphalt is a oil tanker built in 2017 measuring approximately 160 meters in length and has a deadweight of 17,764 metric tons. It flies the flag of the Marshall Islands and is owned and commercially operated by Nave Shipping SA, a company registered in Liberia. Its maintenance, technical and safety operations are overseen by Singapore-based Thome Ship Management, according to online records.

The vessel, which had a next recorded destination for Singapore, does not appear on the international sanctions lists checked by maritime tracking services, including Magic Port.

Sebagaimana diketahui, however, it was previously fined c$7,800 by canadian authorities for a violation of the canada shipping act and related vessel pollution regulations. The penalty, recorded on 11 August 2020, stemmed from an officer failing to properly carry out their duties while supervising a transfer operation aboard the oil tanker, according to the Canadian government.

Louisiana’s governor, Jeff Landry, on Friday afternoon said he was headed to New Orleans.

#483. As Van Hollen wages a challenge, Senate Democrats are torn on whom to elect as their leader

📅 13 Nov 2026

As Van Hollen wages a challenge, Senate Democrats are torn on whom to elect as their leader

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/13/democrats-midterms-senate-leader

Maryland senator’s bid against Chuck Schumer for leadership could decide direction of the Democratic party.

Ever since Donald Trump returned to the White House, Democratic officeholders and voters alike have been divided over whether their leader in the Senate, Chuck Schumer, is up to the task of taking the president on.

That debate intensified on Thursday, when the Maryland senator Chris Van Hollen announced he will challenge Schumer for the post of Democratic Senate leader, which will become one of the most powerful jobs in Washington when the party takes control of Congress’s upper chamber next year.

Diungkapkan bahwa the contest between schumer and van hollen is the party’s first major test of unity after its triumph in last week’s midterm elections, in which voters gave democrats their biggest majorities in both the senate and house of representatives in years. Now the party will be forced to confront the two veteran lawmakers’ differing visions on how to use their newly expanded power to confront Trump, advance the party’s agenda and address divisive issues such as the question of aid to Israel.

Diungkapkan bahwa “trump’s policies have been fired, but we are still in the position where we need to take advantage of this opportunity. So that does mean closing the trust deficit? … And I don’t think you can close the trust deficit by simply returning to the status quo,” Van Hollen said at a press conference on Friday.

Berdasarkan laporan, progressive groups have cheered the 67-year-old van hollen’s candidacy, and he’s picked up a handful of endorsements in the hours since he made his bid official. But his prospects are unclear: the senator said he is an “underdog” in the contest, which is set to be decided at a behind-closed-doors caucus meeting scheduled for 1 December.

Schumer, meanwhile, has expressed confidence he’ll win the Democratic caucus’s nod again, and has the support of senators from across the party’s ideological spectrum.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i welcome any discussion about the future of our caucus and the important work ahead,” schumer, 75, wrote on x after van hollen announced his bid. “I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a new york city native, schumer won election to the house in 1980, then the senate in 1998. He became the top Senate Democrat in 2017, when the party was in the minority at the beginning of Trump’s first term. Four years later, Schumer became majority leader under Joe Biden, and managed to win passage of parts of his legislative agenda even though the Democratic caucus was so small it could not lose a single vote on party-line bills.

Sebagaimana diketahui, trump returned to power in 2025, and it was not long after that schumer’s leadership came into question. In March of that year, Congress faced a deadline to approve new government funding or cause a shutdown. Though many Democrats believed they had leverage over Trump to win concessions, perhaps over the gutting of the federal government by the “department of government efficiency”, Schumer opted to advance a GOP-backed spending measure, arguing that it was a bad time to shut down the government.

The compromise triggered an explosion of anger at Schumer both from Democrats in the House of Representatives who had rejected the funding compromise, and activist groups who saw it as a sign that Schumer was no longer fit to be leader.

Diungkapkan bahwa “senator schumer has contributed to and led many important accomplishments that indivisible is grateful for. But with our democracy on the line, he let us, the country and the Democratic party down,” said Ezra Levin, co-executive director of the network of progressive groups.

Berdasarkan laporan, “senator schumer should step aside as leader. Every Democrat in the Senate should call for him to do so, and begin making plans for new leadership immediately. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, the relationship between schumer and the party base – including some democratic lawmakers – has yet to recover. Another wave of calls for Schumer to step down arrived later that year, when dissident Senate Democrats decided to end a record-long government shutdown without Republicans meeting any of their demands on healthcare.

Diungkapkan bahwa schumer did not publicly endorse their deal, but it was widely believed to have his backing. By the time campaigning for the 2026 midterms began, several candidates were making their opposition to him prominent in their platforms.

Berdasarkan laporan, in some ways, the tension is a unique consequence of the differences in power between the minority party in the house and senate. In the former, the party out of power has little recourse to block legislation, but in the latter, the filibuster’s 60-vote threshold makes Schumer a major figure in deciding whether his party plays along with the 53 Republicans in the majority, or obstructs them.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, at the same time that schumer’s standing among democrats was growing rocky, van hollen’s star was ascending. Elected to the Senate from the House in 2016, Van Hollen made national news when he traveled to El Salvador to meet Kilmar Ábrego García, a Salvadorian who had been wrongfully deported from Maryland in the early days of Trump’s mass deportation campaign.

A deep dive into the policies, controversies and oddities surrounding the Trump administration.

Diungkapkan bahwa he has joined in criticizing israel, amid a wider backlash among democratic voters towards the us ally fueled by accusations it committed a genocide in gaza. Van Hollen voted against providing bulldozers and bombs to the country, and after a visit to the Gaza-Egypt border in 2025, co-released a report accusing Israel of planning to ethnically cleanse the territory. In September, the senator led an unsuccessful resolution to force the state department to issue a report on violence in the West Bank.

Berdasarkan laporan, schumer’s criticism of israel has been comparatively muted – he did not vote for the efforts to cute off arm sales, but did support van hollen’s resolution on the state department report. When he was majority leader in 2024, and thereby the highest-ranking Jewish official in the US government, Schumer called on the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, to step aside.

Sebagaimana diketahui, last week’s sweep of the midterm elections seems to vindicate his leadership of senate democrats – after all, the party won just about every state it was contesting, and some where it had invested few resources. Yet Van Hollen said Schumer could have done better, noting that several candidates he had backed in the primaries wound up being rejected by voters.

Diungkapkan bahwa after the election, reports emerged that van hollen was not planning to challenge schumer, fueling speculation that he would instead run for president in 2028. He now says he’s not interested in a presidential run, and announced the bid for party leader just as activists again called for Senate Democrats to replace Schumer.

“Our members are tired of politicians content with incrementalism – they want bold, creative leadership that will help Democrats usher in affordability and accountability without delay or compromise in the next Congress,” said Joel Payne, the executive director of liberal group MoveOn.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “we welcome and will support any potential senate leader willing to meet the moment. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a small number of democratic senators have publicly backed van hollen since he announced his leadership bid, including bernie sanders, the independent progressive who caucuses with the party, and incoming senators abdul el-sayed of michigan and peggy flanagan of minnesota. Others, such as Elissa Slotkin of Michigan, incoming senator Adam Hamilton of Kansas and Juliana Stratton of Illinois, said the party should choose a new leader, but have not said who that should be.

Diungkapkan bahwa schumer, meanwhile, retains considerable sway in the party, and has been endorsed by progressive and moderate senators alike. Those who have backed him argue he’s been effective, and point to last week’s results as proof.

“Why would you fire the manager when you just won the World Series?” asked Angus King, the Maine independent who caucuses with the Democrats, and endorsed Schumer.
